*הלוך **הוֹלֵ֣ךְ אֶת־חֲכָמִ֣ים *וחכם **יֶחְכָּ֑ם וְרֹעֶ֖ה כְסִילִ֣ים יֵרֽוֹעַ׃
Trouble pursues sinners, but good rewards the righteous.
חַ֭טָּאִים תְּרַדֵּ֣ף רָעָ֑ה וְאֶת־צַ֝דִּיקִ֗ים יְשַׁלֶּם־טֽוֹב׃
A good person leaves an inheritance to his grandchildren, but the sinner's wealth is stored up for the righteous.
ט֗וֹב יַנְחִ֥יל בְּנֵֽי־בָנִ֑ים וְצָפ֥וּן לַ֝צַּדִּ֗יק חֵ֣יל חוֹטֵֽא׃
The unplowed field of the poor yields much food, but it is swept away by injustice.[^20]
רָב־אֹ֖[d]כֶל נִ֣יר רָאשִׁ֑ים וְיֵ֥שׁ נִ֝סְפֶּ֗ה בְּלֹ֣א מִשְׁפָּֽט׃
Whoever spares his rod hates his son, but whoever loves him is careful to discipline him.
חוֹשֵׂ֣ךְ שִׁ֭בְטוֹ שׂוֹנֵ֣א בְנ֑וֹ וְ֝אֹהֲב֗וֹ שִֽׁחֲר֥וֹ מוּסָֽר׃
The righteous eats until he is satisfied, but the stomach of the wicked goes hungry.
צַדִּ֗יק אֹ֭כֵל לְשֹׂ֣בַע נַפְשׁ֑וֹ וּבֶ֖טֶן רְשָׁעִ֣ים תֶּחְסָֽר׃ פ

n.1: Literally "A wise son, a father's discipline". Hebrew *musar*: discipline, training and correction (see 1:2). Also in verses 18 and 24.
n.2: Hebrew *lets*: one who scorns wisdom and laughs at correction (see 1:22).
n.3: Literally "but the appetite (*nephesh*) of the treacherous, violence".
n.4: Hebrew *atsel*, traditionally "sluggard" (see 6:6).
n.5: Literally "the appetite (*nephesh*) of the diligent will be made fat".
n.6: Hebrew *tsaddiq*: one who does what is right (see 2:20).
n.7: Hebrew *rasha*: one who is guilty of wrong (see 2:22).
n.8: Or "make themselves a stench and a disgrace".
n.9: Literally "overthrows sin".
n.10: Literally "rejoices".
n.11: Literally "from a breath (*hevel*)", that is, gained without effort or by dishonest means. The Septuagint reads "Wealth gained in haste".
n.12: Or "will be held in pledge by it".
n.13: Hebrew *sekhel tov*, "good sense".
n.14: Hebrew *eitan*, usually "lasting, enduring"; here perhaps "hard, rough". The Septuagint reads "leads to ruin".
n.15: Hebrew *arum*, "shrewd, prudent" (see 1:4).
n.17: Hebrew *iwwelet*, "folly", the word related to *ewil*, "fool" (see 1:7).
n.18: The Hebrew text is written "Walk with the wise and become wise" but read "Whoever walks with the wise becomes wise".
n.19: In Hebrew there is a play on words: *ro'eh*, "companion", and *yero'a*, "will suffer harm".
n.20: The Hebrew of this verse is difficult. Literally "Much food, the fallow ground of the poor, but there is what is swept away without justice".

v: The wise woman builds her house,[^1] but folly[^2] tears it down with her own hands.
חַכְמ֣וֹת נָ֭שִׁים בָּנְתָ֣ה בֵיתָ֑הּ וְ֝אִוֶּ֗לֶת בְּיָדֶ֥יהָ תֶהֶרְסֶֽנּוּ׃
Whoever walks uprightly fears the LORD,[^3] but whoever is devious in his ways despises him.
הוֹלֵ֣ךְ בְּ֭יָשְׁרוֹ יְרֵ֣א יְהוָ֑ה וּנְל֖וֹז דְּרָכָ֣יו בּוֹזֵֽהוּ׃
In the mouth of a fool[^4] is a rod for his pride,[^5] but the lips of the wise protect them.
בְּֽפִי־אֱ֭וִיל חֹ֣טֶר גַּאֲוָ֑ה וְשִׂפְתֵ֥י חֲ֝כָמִ֗ים תִּשְׁמוּרֵֽם׃
Where there are no oxen, the manger is clean,[^6] but much produce comes by the strength of an ox.
בְּאֵ֣ין אֲ֭לָפִים אֵב֣וּס בָּ֑ר וְרָב־תְּ֝בוּא֗וֹת בְּכֹ֣חַ שֽׁוֹר׃
A faithful witness does not lie, but a false witness breathes out lies.
עֵ֣ד אֱ֭מוּנִים לֹ֣א יְכַזֵּ֑ב וְיָפִ֥יחַ כְּ֝זָבִ֗ים עֵ֣ד שָֽׁקֶר׃
A mocker[^7] seeks wisdom and finds none, but knowledge comes easily to the discerning.
בִּקֶּשׁ־לֵ֣ץ חָכְמָ֣ה וָאָ֑יִן וְדַ֖עַת לְנָב֣וֹן נָקָֽל׃
Leave the presence of a fool,[^8] for you will not find words of knowledge on his lips.
לֵ֣ךְ מִ֭נֶּגֶד לְאִ֣ישׁ כְּסִ֑יל וּבַל־יָ֝דַ֗עְתָּ שִׂפְתֵי־דָֽעַת׃
The wisdom of the prudent[^9] is to understand his way, but the folly of fools is deceit.
חָכְמַ֣ת עָ֭רוּם הָבִ֣ין דַּרְכּ֑וֹ וְאִוֶּ֖לֶת כְּסִילִ֣ים מִרְמָֽה׃
Fools mock at making amends,[^10] but among the upright there is goodwill.
אֱ֭וִלִים יָלִ֣יץ אָשָׁ֑ם וּבֵ֖ין יְשָׁרִ֣ים רָצֽוֹן׃
The heart knows its own bitterness, and no stranger shares in its joy.
לֵ֗ב י֭וֹדֵעַ מָרַּ֣ת נַפְשׁ֑וֹ וּ֝בְשִׂמְחָת֗וֹ לֹא־יִתְעָ֥רַב זָֽר׃
The house of the wicked[^11] will be destroyed, but the tent of the upright will flourish.
בֵּ֣ית רְ֭שָׁעִים יִשָּׁמֵ֑ד וְאֹ֖הֶל יְשָׁרִ֣ים יַפְרִֽיחַ׃
There is a way that seems right to a person, but in the end it leads to death.[^12]
יֵ֤שׁ דֶּ֣רֶךְ יָ֭שָׁר לִפְנֵי־אִ֑ישׁ וְ֝אַחֲרִיתָ֗הּ דַּרְכֵי־מָֽוֶת׃
Even in laughter the heart may ache, and joy may end in grief.
גַּם־בִּשְׂח֥וֹק יִכְאַב־לֵ֑ב וְאַחֲרִיתָ֖הּ שִׂמְחָ֣ה תוּגָֽה׃
The faithless in heart will have his fill of his own ways, and a good person of what is his.[^13]
מִדְּרָכָ֣יו יִ֭שְׂבַּע ס֣וּג לֵ֑ב וּ֝מֵעָלָ֗יו אִ֣ישׁ טֽוֹב׃
The simple[^14] believe everything, but the prudent watch their steps.
פֶּ֭תִי יַאֲמִ֣ין לְכָל־דָּבָ֑ר וְ֝עָר֗וּם יָבִ֥ין לַאֲשֻׁרֽוֹ׃
The wise is cautious[^15] and turns away from evil, but a fool is reckless and overconfident.
חָכָ֣ם יָ֭רֵא וְסָ֣ר מֵרָ֑ע וּ֝כְסִ֗יל מִתְעַבֵּ֥ר וּבוֹטֵֽחַ׃
A quick-tempered person does foolish things, and a man of schemes[^16] is hated.
קְֽצַר־אַ֭פַּיִם יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה אִוֶּ֑לֶת וְאִ֥ישׁ מְ֝זִמּ֗וֹת יִשָּׂנֵֽא׃
The simple inherit folly, but the prudent are crowned with knowledge.
נָחֲל֣וּ פְתָאיִ֣ם אִוֶּ֑לֶת וַֽ֝עֲרוּמִ֗ים יַכְתִּ֥רוּ דָֽעַת׃
The evil bow down before the good, and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.[^17]
שַׁח֣וּ רָ֭עִים לִפְנֵ֣י טוֹבִ֑ים וּ֝רְשָׁעִ֗ים עַֽל־שַׁעֲרֵ֥י צַדִּֽיק׃
The poor are disliked even by their neighbors, but the rich have many friends.
גַּם־לְ֭רֵעֵהוּ יִשָּׂ֣נֵא רָ֑שׁ וְאֹהֲבֵ֖י עָשִׁ֣יר רַבִּֽים׃
Whoever despises his neighbor sins, but happy[^18] is the one who is kind to the humble.[^19]
בָּז־לְרֵעֵ֥הוּ חוֹטֵ֑א וּמְחוֹנֵ֖ן *עניים **עֲנָוִ֣ים אַשְׁרָֽיו׃
Do not those who plot evil go astray? But faithful love and truth[^20] belong to those who plan good.
הֲ‍ֽלוֹא־יִ֭תְעוּ חֹ֣רְשֵׁי רָ֑ע וְחֶ֥סֶד וֶ֝אֱמֶ֗ת חֹ֣רְשֵׁי טֽוֹב׃
In all hard work there is profit, but mere talk leads only to poverty.
בְּכָל־עֶ֭צֶב יִהְיֶ֣ה מוֹתָ֑ר וּדְבַר־שְׂ֝פָתַ֗יִם אַךְ־לְמַחְסֽוֹר׃
The crown of the wise is their wealth, but the folly of fools is folly.
עֲטֶ֣רֶת חֲכָמִ֣ים עָשְׁרָ֑ם אִוֶּ֖לֶת כְּסִילִ֣ים אִוֶּֽלֶת׃
A truthful witness saves lives, but one who breathes out lies is a deceiver.
מַצִּ֣יל נְ֭פָשׁוֹת עֵ֣ד אֱמֶ֑ת וְיָפִ֖חַ כְּזָבִ֣ים מִרְמָֽה׃
In the fear of the LORD there is strong confidence, and his children will have a refuge.
בְּיִרְאַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה מִבְטַח־עֹ֑ז וּ֝לְבָנָ֗יו יִהְיֶ֥ה מַחְסֶֽה׃
The fear of the LORD is a fountain of life, for turning away from the snares of death.
יִרְאַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה מְק֣וֹר חַיִּ֑ים לָ֝ס֗וּר מִמֹּ֥קְשֵׁי מָֽוֶת׃
In a multitude of people is a king's glory, but without people a ruler is ruined.
בְּרָב־עָ֥ם הַדְרַת־מֶ֑לֶךְ וּבְאֶ֥פֶס לְ֝אֹ֗ם מְחִתַּ֥ת רָזֽוֹן׃
Whoever is slow to anger has great insight,[^21] but whoever is quick-tempered displays folly.
אֶ֣רֶךְ אַ֭פַּיִם רַב־תְּבוּנָ֑ה וּקְצַר־ר֝֗וּחַ מֵרִ֥ים אִוֶּֽלֶת׃
A calm heart gives life to the body,[^22] but envy rots the bones.
חַיֵּ֣י בְ֭שָׂרִים לֵ֣ב מַרְפֵּ֑א וּרְקַ֖ב עֲצָמ֣וֹת קִנְאָֽה׃
Whoever oppresses the poor insults his Maker, but whoever is kind to the needy honors him.
עֹ֣שֵֽׁק־דָּ֭ל חֵרֵ֣ף עֹשֵׂ֑הוּ וּ֝מְכַבְּד֗וֹ חֹנֵ֥ן אֶבְיֽוֹן׃
The wicked is thrown down by his own evil, but the righteous finds refuge even in his death.[^23]
בְּֽ֭רָעָתוֹ יִדָּחֶ֣ה רָשָׁ֑ע וְחֹסֶ֖ה בְמוֹת֣וֹ צַדּֽ͏ִיק׃
Wisdom rests in the heart of the discerning, and even among fools she makes herself known.[^24]
בְּלֵ֣ב נָ֭בוֹן תָּנ֣וּחַ חָכְמָ֑ה וּבְקֶ֥רֶב כְּ֝סִילִ֗ים תִּוָּדֵֽעַ׃
Righteousness exalts a nation, but sin is a disgrace[^25] to any people.
צְדָקָ֥ה תְרֽוֹמֵֽם־גּ֑וֹי וְחֶ֖סֶד לְאֻמִּ֣ים חַטָּֽאת׃
A king delights in a servant who acts with good sense,[^26] but his wrath falls on one who acts shamefully.
רְֽצוֹן־מֶ֭לֶךְ לְעֶ֣בֶד מַשְׂכִּ֑יל וְ֝עֶבְרָת֗וֹ תִּהְיֶ֥ה מֵבִֽישׁ׃

n.1: Literally "The wise ones of women has built her house". With different vowels, "Wisdom (*chokhmot*, as in 9:1) has built her house", and the second line would then speak of Folly (compare 9:13).
n.2: Hebrew *iwwelet*, "folly", the word related to *ewil*, "fool" (see 1:7). Also in verses 8, 17, 18, 24 and 29.
n.3: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.4: Hebrew *ewil*, the morally perverse, stubborn fool (see 1:7). Also in verse 9.
n.5: Literally "a rod of pride". The word for *rod* can also mean "shoot, branch" (Isaiah 11:1): his proud words may bring a beating on him, or his mouth sprouts pride.
n.6: Or "the manger is empty of grain".
n.7: Hebrew *lets*: one who scorns wisdom and laughs at correction (see 1:22).
n.8: Hebrew *kesil* (see 1:22). Also in verses 8, 16, 24 and 33.
n.9: Hebrew *arum*, "shrewd, prudent" (see 1:4). Also in verses 15 and 18.
n.10: The Hebrew is difficult. Literally "Fools, he mocks guilt". Hebrew *asham* means "guilt", "making amends" or "guilt offering". Or "Guilt mocks fools".
n.11: Hebrew *resha'im*, plural of *rasha*: those who are guilty of wrong (see 2:22).
n.12: Literally "but its end is ways of death". The verse is repeated in 16:25.
n.13: Literally "and from upon him a good man". Some scholars read "from his deeds", with a small change to the Hebrew.
n.14: Hebrew *peti*: a naive, inexperienced person, easily led (see 1:4). Also in verse 18.
n.15: Literally "fears". Or "fears (the LORD)".
n.17: Hebrew *tsaddiq*: one who does what is right (see 2:20).
n.18: Hebrew *ashrei*: happy, fortunate; traditionally "blessed".
n.19: The Hebrew text is written "the poor" but read "the humble".
n.20: Hebrew *chesed ve-emet*: faithful love and reliability (see 3:3). Literally "faithful love and truth, those who plan good".
n.22: Literally "A heart of healing (or calm) is the life of the flesh".
n.23: The Septuagint reads "but whoever trusts in his own holiness is righteous", probably reading *betummo*, "in his integrity", in place of *bemoto*, "in his death", a word with the same letters in a different order.
n.24: The Septuagint reads "but in the heart of fools it is not known".
n.25: Hebrew *chesed*, here a rarer word meaning "shame, disgrace" (Leviticus 20:17), spelled like the word for "faithful love".

v: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.
מַֽעֲנֶה־רַּ֭ךְ יָשִׁ֣יב חֵמָ֑ה וּדְבַר־עֶ֝֗צֶב יַעֲלֶה־אָֽף׃
The tongue of the wise makes knowledge attractive,[^1] but the mouth of fools[^2] gushes folly.[^3]
לְשׁ֣וֹן חֲ֭כָמִים תֵּיטִ֣יב דָּ֑עַת וּפִ֥י כְ֝סִילִ֗ים יַבִּ֥יעַ אִוֶּֽלֶת׃
The eyes of the LORD[^4] are everywhere, watching the evil and the good.
בְּֽכָל־מָ֭קוֹם עֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה צֹ֝פ֗וֹת רָעִ֥ים וטוֹבִֽים׃
A soothing tongue is a tree of life, but a twisted one crushes the spirit.
מַרְפֵּ֣א לָ֭שׁוֹן עֵ֣ץ חַיִּ֑ים וְסֶ֥לֶף בָּ֝֗הּ שֶׁ֣בֶר בְּרֽוּחַ׃
A fool[^5] despises his father's discipline,[^6] but whoever heeds correction is prudent.[^7]
אֱוִ֗יל יִ֭נְאַץ מוּסַ֣ר אָבִ֑יו וְשֹׁמֵ֖ר תּוֹכַ֣חַת יַעְרִֽם׃
In the house of the righteous[^8] there is great treasure, but the income of the wicked[^9] brings trouble.
בֵּ֣ית צַ֭דִּיק חֹ֣סֶן רָ֑ב וּבִתְבוּאַ֖ת רָשָׁ֣ע נֶעְכָּֽרֶת׃
The lips of the wise spread knowledge, but the heart of fools is not so.[^10]
שִׂפְתֵ֣י חֲ֭כָמִים יְזָ֣רוּ דָ֑עַת וְלֵ֖ב כְּסִילִ֣ים לֹא־כֵֽן׃
The sacrifice of the wicked is detestable to the LORD, but the prayer of the upright is his delight.
זֶ֣בַח רְ֭שָׁעִים תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה וּתְפִלַּ֖ת יְשָׁרִ֣ים רְצוֹנֽוֹ׃
The way of the wicked is detestable to the LORD, but he loves the one who pursues righteousness.
תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה דֶּ֣רֶךְ רָשָׁ֑ע וּמְרַדֵּ֖ף צְדָקָ֣ה יֶאֱהָֽב׃
Severe discipline awaits the one who leaves the path; whoever hates correction will die.
מוּסָ֣ר רָ֭ע לְעֹזֵ֣ב אֹ֑רַח שׂוֹנֵ֖א תוֹכַ֣חַת יָמֽוּת׃
Sheol and Abaddon[^11] lie open before the LORD; how much more the hearts of humankind!
שְׁא֣וֹל וַ֭אֲבַדּוֹן נֶ֣גֶד יְהוָ֑ה אַ֝֗ף כִּֽי־לִבּ֥וֹת בְּֽנֵי־אָדָֽם׃
A mocker[^12] does not love the one who corrects him; he will not go to the wise.
לֹ֣א יֶאֱהַב־לֵ֭ץ הוֹכֵ֣חַֽ ל֑וֹ אֶל־חֲ֝כָמִ֗ים לֹ֣א יֵלֵֽךְ׃
A glad heart makes a cheerful face, but by heartache the spirit is crushed.
לֵ֣ב שָׂ֭מֵחַ יֵיטִ֣ב פָּנִ֑ים וּבְעַצְּבַת־לֵ֝ב ר֣וּחַ נְכֵאָֽה׃
The heart of the discerning seeks knowledge, but the mouth of fools[^13] feeds on folly.
לֵ֣ב נָ֭בוֹן יְבַקֶּשׁ־דָּ֑עַת *ופני **וּפִ֥י כְ֝סִילִ֗ים יִרְעֶ֥ה אִוֶּֽלֶת׃
All the days of the poor are hard, but a cheerful heart has a continual feast.
כָּל־יְמֵ֣י עָנִ֣י רָעִ֑ים וְטֽוֹב־לֵ֝֗ב מִשְׁתֶּ֥ה תָמִֽיד׃
Better a little with the fear of the LORD than great treasure with turmoil.
טוֹב־מְ֭עַט בְּיִרְאַ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה מֵאוֹצָ֥ר רָ֝֗ב וּמְה֥וּמָה בֽוֹ׃
Better a meal of vegetables where there is love than a fattened ox with hatred.
ט֤וֹב אֲרֻחַ֣ת יָ֭רָק וְאַהֲבָה־שָׁ֑ם מִשּׁ֥וֹר אָ֝ב֗וּס וְשִׂנְאָה־בֽוֹ׃
A hot-tempered man stirs up strife, but one who is slow to anger calms a quarrel.
אִ֣ישׁ חֵ֭מָה יְגָרֶ֣ה מָד֑וֹן וְאֶ֥רֶך אַ֝פַּ֗יִם יַשְׁקִ֥יט רִֽיב׃
The way of the lazy person[^14] is like a hedge of thorns, but the path of the upright is a highway.
דֶּ֣רֶךְ עָ֭צֵל כִּמְשֻׂ֣כַת חָ֑דֶק וְאֹ֖רַח יְשָׁרִ֣ים סְלֻלָֽה׃
A wise son makes a father glad, but a foolish man despises his mother.
בֵּ֣ן חָ֭כָם יְשַׂמַּח־אָ֑ב וּכְסִ֥יל אָ֝דָ֗ם בּוֹזֶ֥ה אִמּֽוֹ׃
Folly is a joy to one who lacks sense,[^15] but a person of insight[^16] walks straight ahead.
אִ֭וֶּלֶת שִׂמְחָ֣ה לַחֲסַר־לֵ֑ב וְאִ֥ישׁ תְּ֝בוּנָ֗ה יְיַשֶׁר־לָֽכֶת׃
Plans fail without counsel, but with many advisers they succeed.
הָפֵ֣ר מַ֭חֲשָׁבוֹת בְּאֵ֣ין ס֑וֹד וּבְרֹ֖ב יוֹעֲצִ֣ים תָּקֽוּם׃
A person finds joy in giving an apt answer, and a word at the right time, how good it is!
שִׂמְחָ֣ה לָ֭אִישׁ בְּמַעֲנֵה־פִ֑יו וְדָבָ֖ר בְּעִתּ֣וֹ מַה־טּֽוֹב׃
The path of life leads upward for the sensible,[^17] so that he may turn away from Sheol below.
אֹ֣רַח חַ֭יִּים לְמַ֣עְלָה לְמַשְׂכִּ֑יל לְמַ֥עַן ס֝֗וּר מִשְּׁא֥וֹל מָֽטָּה׃
The LORD tears down the house of the proud, but he sets firm the boundary of the widow.
בֵּ֣ית גֵּ֭אִים יִסַּ֥ח ׀ יְהוָ֑ה וְ֝יַצֵּ֗ב גְּב֣וּל אַלְמָנָֽה׃
Evil plans are detestable to the LORD, but gracious words are pure.[^18]
תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה מַחְשְׁב֣וֹת רָ֑ע וּ֝טְהֹרִ֗ים אִמְרֵי־נֹֽעַם׃
Whoever is greedy for gain brings trouble on his household, but whoever hates bribes will live.
עֹכֵ֣ר בֵּ֭יתוֹ בּוֹצֵ֣עַ בָּ֑צַע וְשׂוֹנֵ֖א מַתָּנֹ֣ת יִחְיֶֽה׃
The heart of the righteous ponders how to answer, but the mouth of the wicked gushes evil things.
לֵ֣ב צַ֭דִּיק יֶהְגֶּ֣ה לַעֲנ֑וֹת וּפִ֥י רְ֝שָׁעִ֗ים יַבִּ֥יעַ רָעֽוֹת׃
The LORD is far from the wicked, but he hears the prayer of the righteous.
רָח֣וֹק יְ֭הוָה מֵרְשָׁעִ֑ים וּתְפִלַּ֖ת צַדִּיקִ֣ים יִשְׁמָֽע׃
Bright eyes[^19] gladden the heart; good news refreshes the bones.[^20]
מְֽאוֹר־עֵ֭ינַיִם יְשַׂמַּֽח־לֵ֑ב שְׁמוּעָ֥ה ט֝וֹבָ֗ה תְּדַשֶּׁן־עָֽצֶם׃
The ear that listens to life-giving correction will live among the wise.
אֹ֗זֶן שֹׁ֖[d]מַעַת תּוֹכַ֣חַת חַיִּ֑ים בְּקֶ֖רֶב חֲכָמִ֣ים תָּלִֽין׃
Whoever ignores discipline despises himself, but whoever listens to correction gains sense.[^21]
פּוֹרֵ֣עַ מ֭וּסָר מוֹאֵ֣ס נַפְשׁ֑וֹ וְשׁוֹמֵ֥עַ תּ֝וֹכַ֗חַת ק֣וֹנֶה לֵּֽב׃
The fear of the LORD is the discipline of wisdom,[^22] and humility comes before honor.
יִרְאַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה מוּסַ֣ר חָכְמָ֑ה וְלִפְנֵ֖י כָב֣וֹד עֲנָוָֽה׃

n.1: Or "uses knowledge well".
n.2: Hebrew *kesilim*, plural of *kesil* (see 1:22). Also in verses 7, 14 and 20.
n.3: Hebrew *iwwelet*, "folly", the word related to *ewil*, "fool" (see 1:7). Also in verses 14 and 21.
n.4: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.5: Hebrew *ewil*, the morally perverse, stubborn fool (see 1:7).
n.6: Hebrew *musar*: discipline, training and correction (see 1:2). Also in verses 10, 32 and 33.
n.7: Hebrew *ya'rim*, a verb from the same root as *ormah*, "shrewdness, prudence" (see 1:4).
n.8: Hebrew *tsaddiq*: one who does what is right (see 2:20).
n.9: Hebrew *rasha*: one who is guilty of wrong (see 2:22).
n.10: Or "is not steady".
n.11: Hebrew *Sheol*, the realm of the dead, and *Abaddon*, "Destruction", another name for it (Job 26:6; 28:22). Also in verse 24.
n.12: Hebrew *lets*: one who scorns wisdom and laughs at correction (see 1:22).
n.13: The Hebrew text is written "the face of fools" but read "the mouth of fools".
n.14: Hebrew *atsel*, traditionally "sluggard" (see 6:6).
n.15: Literally "lacks heart". In Hebrew thought the heart is the seat of understanding.
n.17: Hebrew *maskil*, as in 10:5.
n.18: Or "but pleasant words are pure in his sight".

v: The plans of the heart belong to people, but the answer of the tongue comes from the LORD.[^1]
לְאָדָ֥ם מַֽעַרְכֵי־לֵ֑ב וּ֝מֵיְהוָ֗ה מַעֲנֵ֥ה לָשֽׁוֹן׃
All a person's ways seem pure in his own eyes, but the LORD weighs the spirits.[^2]
כָּֽל־דַּרְכֵי־אִ֭ישׁ זַ֣ךְ בְּעֵינָ֑יו וְתֹכֵ֖ן רוּח֣וֹת יְהוָֽה׃
Commit your works to the LORD,[^3] and your plans will be established.
גֹּ֣ל אֶל־יְהוָ֣ה מַעֲשֶׂ֑יךָ וְ֝יִכֹּ֗נוּ מַחְשְׁבֹתֶֽיךָ׃
The LORD has made everything for its purpose,[^4] even the wicked[^5] for the day of disaster.
כֹּ֤ל פָּעַ֣ל יְ֭הוָה לַֽמַּעֲנֵ֑הוּ וְגַם־רָ֝שָׁ֗ע לְי֣וֹם רָעָֽה׃
Everyone who is proud in heart is detestable to the LORD; you can be sure[^6] he will not go unpunished.
תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה כָּל־גְּבַהּ־לֵ֑ב יָ֥ד לְ֝יָ֗ד לֹ֣א יִנָּקֶֽה׃
By faithful love and truth[^7] iniquity is atoned for,[^8] and by the fear of the LORD one turns away from evil.
בְּחֶ֣סֶד וֶ֭אֱמֶת יְכֻפַּ֣ר עָוֺ֑ן וּבְיִרְאַ֥ת יְ֝הוָ֗ה ס֣וּר מֵרָֽע׃
When a person's ways please the LORD, he makes even his enemies be at peace with him.
בִּרְצ֣וֹת יְ֭הוָה דַּרְכֵי־אִ֑ישׁ גַּם־א֝וֹיְבָ֗יו יַשְׁלִ֥ם אִתּֽוֹ׃
Better a little with righteousness than great income with injustice.
טוֹב־מְ֭עַט בִּצְדָקָ֑ה מֵרֹ֥ב תְּ֝בוּא֗וֹת בְּלֹ֣א מִשְׁפָּֽט׃
A person's heart plans his way, but the LORD directs his steps.
לֵ֣ב אָ֭דָם יְחַשֵּׁ֣ב דַּרְכּ֑וֹ וַֽ֝יהוָ֗ה יָכִ֥ין צַעֲדֽוֹ׃
Inspired decisions[^9] are on the lips of a king; his mouth does not betray justice.
קֶ֤סֶם ׀ עַֽל־שִׂפְתֵי־מֶ֑לֶךְ בְּ֝מִשְׁפָּ֗ט לֹ֣א יִמְעַל־פִּֽיו׃
Honest balances and scales belong to the LORD; all the weights in the bag are his work.
פֶּ֤לֶס ׀ וּמֹאזְנֵ֣י מִ֭שְׁפָּט לַֽיהוָ֑ה מַ֝עֲשֵׂ֗הוּ כָּל־אַבְנֵי־כִֽיס׃
Doing wickedness is detestable to kings,[^10] for a throne is established by righteousness.
תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת מְ֭לָכִים עֲשׂ֣וֹת רֶ֑שַׁע כִּ֥י בִ֝צְדָקָ֗ה יִכּ֥וֹן כִּסֵּֽא׃
Righteous lips are the delight of kings, and they love one who speaks what is right.
רְצ֣וֹן מְ֭לָכִים שִׂפְתֵי־צֶ֑דֶק וְדֹבֵ֖ר יְשָׁרִ֣ים יֶאֱהָֽב׃
A king's wrath is a messenger of death, but a wise person will appease it.
חֲמַת־מֶ֥לֶךְ מַלְאֲכֵי־מָ֑וֶת וְאִ֖ישׁ חָכָ֣ם יְכַפְּרֶֽנָּה׃
In the light of a king's face is life, and his favor is like a cloud that brings the spring rain.[^11]
בְּאוֹר־פְּנֵי־מֶ֥לֶךְ חַיִּ֑ים וּ֝רְצוֹנ֗וֹ כְּעָ֣ב מַלְקֽוֹשׁ׃
How much better to get wisdom than gold! To get understanding[^12] is better than silver.
קְֽנֹה־חָכְמָ֗ה מַה־טּ֥וֹב מֵחָר֑וּץ וּקְנ֥וֹת בִּ֝ינָ֗ה נִבְחָ֥ר מִכָּֽסֶף׃
The highway of the upright turns away from evil; whoever watches his way preserves his life.
מְסִלַּ֣ת יְ֭שָׁרִים ס֣וּר מֵרָ֑ע שֹׁמֵ֥ר נַ֝פְשׁ֗וֹ נֹצֵ֥ר דַּרְכּֽוֹ׃
Pride comes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.
לִפְנֵי־שֶׁ֥בֶר גָּא֑וֹן וְלִפְנֵ֥י כִ֝שָּׁל֗וֹן גֹּ֣בַהּ רֽוּחַ׃
Better to be lowly in spirit with the humble[^13] than to divide plunder with the proud.
ט֣וֹב שְׁפַל־ר֭וּחַ אֶת־*עניים **עֲנָוִ֑ים מֵֽחַלֵּ֥ק שָׁ֝לָ֗ל אֶת־גֵּאִֽים׃
Whoever pays attention to the word[^14] will find good, and happy[^15] is the one who trusts in the LORD.
מַשְׂכִּ֣יל עַל־דָּ֭בָר יִמְצָא־ט֑וֹב וּבוֹטֵ֖חַ בַּיהוָ֣ה אַשְׁרָֽיו׃
The wise in heart are called discerning, and sweet speech increases learning.[^16]
לַחֲכַם־לֵ֭ב יִקָּרֵ֣א נָב֑וֹן וּמֶ֥תֶק שְׂ֝פָתַ֗יִם יֹסִ֥יף לֶֽקַח׃
Good sense[^17] is a fountain of life to those who have it, but folly is the discipline of fools.[^18]
מְק֣וֹר חַ֭יִּים שֵׂ֣כֶל בְּעָלָ֑יו וּמוּסַ֖ר אֱוִלִ֣ים אִוֶּֽלֶת׃
The heart of the wise makes his mouth wise and adds learning to his lips.
לֵ֣ב חָ֭כָם יַשְׂכִּ֣יל פִּ֑יהוּ וְעַל־שְׂ֝פָתָ֗יו יֹסִ֥יף לֶֽקַח׃
Pleasant words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul and healing to the bones.
צוּף־דְּ֭בַשׁ אִמְרֵי־נֹ֑עַם מָת֥וֹק לַ֝נֶּפֶשׁ וּמַרְפֵּ֥א לָעָֽצֶם׃
There is a way that seems right to a person, but in the end it leads to death.[^19]
יֵ֤שׁ דֶּ֣רֶךְ יָ֭שָׁר לִפְנֵי־אִ֑ישׁ וְ֝אַחֲרִיתָ֗הּ דַּרְכֵי־מָֽוֶת׃
A worker's appetite works for him, for his hunger[^20] drives him on.
נֶ֣פֶשׁ עָ֭מֵל עָ֣מְלָה לּ֑וֹ כִּֽי־אָכַ֖ף עָלָ֣יו פִּֽיהוּ׃
A worthless man[^21] digs up evil, and on his lips it is like a scorching fire.
אִ֣ישׁ בְּ֭לִיַּעַל כֹּרֶ֣ה רָעָ֑ה וְעַל־*שפתיו **שְׂ֝פָת֗וֹ כְּאֵ֣שׁ צָרָֽבֶת׃
A perverse person spreads strife, and a gossip[^22] separates close friends.
אִ֣ישׁ תַּ֭הְפֻּכוֹת יְשַׁלַּ֣ח מָד֑וֹן וְ֝נִרְגָּ֗ן[6] מַפְרִ֥יד אַלּֽוּף׃
A violent man entices his neighbor and leads him in a way that is not good.
אִ֣ישׁ חָ֭מָס יְפַתֶּ֣ה רֵעֵ֑הוּ וְ֝הוֹלִיכ֗וֹ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ לֹא־טֽוֹב׃
Whoever winks his eyes is plotting perversity; whoever purses his lips has brought evil about.
עֹצֶ֣ה עֵ֭ינָיו לַחְשֹׁ֣ב תַּהְפֻּכ֑וֹת קֹרֵ֥ץ שְׂ֝פָתָ֗יו כִּלָּ֥ה רָעָֽה׃
Gray hair is a glorious crown; it is found in the way of righteousness.
עֲטֶ֣רֶת תִּפְאֶ֣רֶת שֵׂיבָ֑ה בְּדֶ֥רֶךְ צְ֝דָקָ֗ה תִּמָּצֵֽא׃
Better to be slow to anger than a mighty warrior, and to rule one's spirit than to capture a city.
ט֤וֹב אֶ֣רֶךְ אַ֭פַּיִם מִגִּבּ֑וֹר וּמֹשֵׁ֥ל בְּ֝רוּח֗וֹ מִלֹּכֵ֥ד עִֽיר׃
The lot is cast into the lap, but its every decision is from the LORD.
בַּ֭חֵיק יוּטַ֣ל אֶת־הַגּוֹרָ֑ל וּ֝מֵיְהוָ֗ה כָּל־מִשְׁפָּטֽוֹ׃

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.2: Or "the motives". Hebrew *ruchot*, plural of *ruach*.
n.3: Literally "Roll your works onto the LORD".
n.4: Or "for himself".
n.5: Hebrew *rasha*: one who is guilty of wrong (see 2:22).
n.6: Literally "hand to hand", as in 11:21.
n.7: Hebrew *chesed ve-emet*: faithful love and reliability (see 3:3).
n.8: Literally "is covered". Hebrew *kipper*, the verb used for making atonement in the sacrifices (Leviticus 16:30).
n.9: Hebrew *qesem*, "divination", elsewhere forbidden (Deuteronomy 18:10); here a decision given as if with divine authority.
n.10: Or "It is detestable for kings to do wickedness".
n.11: Hebrew *malqosh*, the late rain of spring that ripened the crops.
n.12: Hebrew *binah*, as in 1:2.
n.13: The Hebrew text is written "with the poor" but read "with the humble".
n.14: Or "Whoever handles a matter wisely". Hebrew *maskil*, as in 10:5.
n.15: Hebrew *ashrei*: happy, fortunate; traditionally "blessed".
n.16: Hebrew *leqach*, "learning", as in 1:5, or "persuasiveness" (7:21). Also in verse 23. Literally "sweetness of lips".
n.17: Hebrew *sekhel*, "good sense, insight".
n.18: Or "but fools are disciplined by their own folly". Literally "and the discipline (*musar*) of fools (*ewilim*) is folly (*iwwelet*)". On *ewil*, see 1:7.
n.22: Hebrew *nirgan*, "whisperer". In the Hebrew text one letter of this word is written small, a scribal mark.

v: Better a dry crust with peace and quiet than a house full of feasting[^1] with strife.
ט֤וֹב פַּ֣ת חֲ֭רֵבָה וְשַׁלְוָה־בָ֑הּ מִ֝בַּ֗יִת מָלֵ֥א זִבְחֵי־רִֽיב׃
A servant who acts wisely[^2] will rule over a son who acts shamefully, and will share the inheritance among the brothers.
עֶֽבֶד־מַשְׂכִּ֗יל יִ֭מְשֹׁל בְּבֵ֣ן מֵבִ֑ישׁ וּבְת֥וֹךְ אַ֝חִ֗ים יַחֲלֹ֥ק נַחֲלָֽה׃
The crucible is for silver and the furnace for gold, but the LORD[^3] tests hearts.
מַצְרֵ֣ף לַ֭כֶּסֶף וְכ֣וּר לַזָּהָ֑ב וּבֹחֵ֖ן לִבּ֣וֹת יְהוָֽה׃
An evildoer listens to wicked lips; a liar pays attention to a destructive tongue.
מֵ֭רַע מַקְשִׁ֣יב עַל־שְׂפַת־אָ֑וֶן שֶׁ֥קֶר מֵ֝זִין עַל־לְשׁ֥וֹן הַוֺּֽת׃
Whoever mocks the poor insults his Maker; whoever rejoices at disaster will not go unpunished.
לֹעֵ֣ג לָ֭רָשׁ חֵרֵ֣ף עֹשֵׂ֑הוּ שָׂמֵ֥חַ לְ֝אֵ֗יד לֹ֣א יִנָּקֶֽה׃
Grandchildren are the crown of the old, and fathers are the glory of their children.
עֲטֶ֣רֶת זְ֭קֵנִים בְּנֵ֣י בָנִ֑ים וְתִפְאֶ֖רֶת בָּנִ֣ים אֲבוֹתָֽם׃
Fine speech is not fitting for a godless fool,[^4] still less are lying lips for a noble.
לֹא־נָאוָ֣ה לְנָבָ֣ל שְׂפַת־יֶ֑תֶר אַ֝֗ף כִּֽי־לְנָדִ֥יב שְׂפַת־שָֽׁקֶר׃
A bribe is a lucky stone[^5] in the eyes of its owner; wherever he turns, he succeeds.
אֶֽבֶן־חֵ֣ן הַ֭שֹּׁחַד בְּעֵינֵ֣י בְעָלָ֑יו אֶֽל־כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֖ר יִפְנֶ֣ה יַשְׂכִּֽיל׃
Whoever covers an offense seeks love, but whoever repeats a matter separates close friends.
מְֽכַסֶּה־פֶּ֭שַׁע מְבַקֵּ֣שׁ אַהֲבָ֑ה וְשֹׁנֶ֥ה בְ֝דָבָ֗ר מַפְרִ֥יד אַלּֽוּף׃
A rebuke goes deeper into a discerning person than a hundred blows into a fool.[^6]
תֵּ֣חַת גְּעָרָ֣ה בְמֵבִ֑ין מֵהַכּ֖וֹת כְּסִ֣יל מֵאָֽה׃
An evil person seeks only rebellion, and a cruel messenger will be sent against him.
אַךְ־מְרִ֥י יְבַקֶּשׁ־רָ֑ע וּמַלְאָ֥ךְ אַ֝כְזָרִ֗י יְשֻׁלַּח־בּֽוֹ׃
Better to meet a bear robbed of her cubs than a fool in his folly.[^7]
פָּג֬וֹשׁ דֹּ֣ב שַׁכּ֣וּל בְּאִ֑ישׁ וְאַל־כְּ֝סִ֗יל בְּאִוַּלְתּֽוֹ׃
Whoever repays good with evil, evil will not leave his house.
מֵשִׁ֣יב רָ֭עָה תַּ֣חַת טוֹבָ֑ה לֹא־*תמיש **תָמ֥וּשׁ רָ֝עָ֗ה מִבֵּיתֽוֹ׃
Starting a quarrel is like letting out water; so drop the dispute before it breaks out.
פּ֣וֹטֵֽר מַ֭יִם רֵאשִׁ֣ית מָד֑וֹן וְלִפְנֵ֥י הִ֝תְגַּלַּ֗ע הָרִ֥יב נְטֽוֹשׁ׃
Whoever acquits the wicked[^8] and whoever condemns the righteous,[^9] both are detestable to the LORD.
מַצְדִּ֣יק רָ֭שָׁע וּמַרְשִׁ֣יעַ צַדִּ֑יק תּוֹעֲבַ֥ת יְ֝הוָ֗ה גַּם־שְׁנֵיהֶֽם׃
Why should a fool have money in his hand to buy wisdom, when he has no sense?[^10]
לָמָּה־זֶּ֣ה מְחִ֣יר בְּיַד־כְּסִ֑יל לִקְנ֖וֹת חָכְמָ֣ה וְלֶב־אָֽיִן׃
A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for times of trouble.
בְּכָל־עֵ֭ת אֹהֵ֣ב הָרֵ֑עַ וְאָ֥ח לְ֝צָרָ֗ה יִוָּלֵֽד׃
One who lacks sense[^11] shakes hands on a pledge and puts up security in front of his neighbor.[^12]
אָדָ֣ם חֲסַר־לֵ֭ב תּוֹקֵ֣עַ כָּ֑ף עֹרֵ֥ב עֲ֝רֻבָּ֗ה לִפְנֵ֥י רֵעֵֽהוּ׃
Whoever loves offense loves strife; whoever makes his doorway high is looking for destruction.[^13]
אֹ֣הֵֽב פֶּ֭שַׁע אֹהֵ֣ב מַצָּ֑ה מַגְבִּ֥יהַּ פִּ֝תְח֗וֹ מְבַקֶּשׁ־שָֽׁבֶר׃
Whoever has a crooked heart finds no good, and whoever has a perverse tongue falls into trouble.
עִקֶּשׁ־לֵ֭ב לֹ֣א יִמְצָא־ט֑וֹב וְנֶהְפָּ֥ךְ בִּ֝לְשׁוֹנ֗וֹ יִפּ֥וֹל בְּרָעָֽה׃
Whoever fathers a fool has grief, and the father of a godless fool has no joy.
יֹלֵ֣ד כְּ֭סִיל לְת֣וּגָה ל֑וֹ וְלֹֽא־יִ֝שְׂמַ֗ח אֲבִ֣י נָבָֽל׃
A glad heart is good medicine,[^14] but a crushed spirit dries up the bones.
לֵ֣ב שָׂ֭מֵחַ יֵיטִ֣ב גֵּהָ֑ה וְר֥וּחַ נְ֝כֵאָ֗ה תְּיַבֶּשׁ־גָּֽרֶם׃
The wicked accepts a bribe in secret[^15] to pervert the paths of justice.
שֹׁ֣חַד מֵ֭חֵיק רָשָׁ֣ע יִקָּ֑ח לְ֝הַטּ֗וֹת אָרְח֥וֹת מִשְׁפָּֽט׃
Wisdom is right in front of the discerning, but the eyes of a fool wander to the ends of the earth.
אֶת־פְּנֵ֣י מֵבִ֣ין חָכְמָ֑ה וְעֵינֵ֥י כְ֝סִ֗יל בִּקְצֵה־אָֽרֶץ׃
A foolish son is a grief to his father and bitterness to the mother who bore him.
כַּ֣עַס לְ֭אָבִיו בֵּ֣ן כְּסִ֑יל וּ֝מֶ֗מֶר לְיוֹלַדְתּֽוֹ׃
It is not good to punish the righteous, or to strike nobles for their uprightness.[^16]
גַּ֤ם עֲנ֣וֹשׁ לַצַּדִּ֣יק לֹּא[t]־ט֑וֹב לְהַכּ֖וֹת נְדִיבִ֣ים עַל־יֹֽשֶׁר׃
Whoever restrains his words has knowledge, and one who is calm in spirit[^17] is a person of insight.[^18]
חוֹשֵׂ֣ךְ אֲ֭מָרָיו יוֹדֵ֣עַ דָּ֑עַת *וקר־**יְקַר־ר֝֗וּחַ אִ֣ישׁ תְּבוּנָֽה׃
Even a fool[^19] who keeps silent is considered wise; whoever closes his lips is thought discerning.
גַּ֤ם אֱוִ֣יל מַ֭חֲרִישׁ חָכָ֣ם יֵחָשֵׁ֑ב אֹטֵ֖ם שְׂפָתָ֣יו נָבֽוֹן׃

n.1: Literally "sacrifices". The meat of some sacrifices was eaten at a feast (7:14).
n.2: Hebrew *maskil*, as in 10:5.
n.3: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.4: Hebrew *nabal*: a senseless, godless person, the word used of Nabal in 1 Samuel 25:25. Also in verse 21.
n.5: Literally "a stone of favor", a charm thought to bring good fortune.
n.6: Hebrew *kesil* (see 1:22). Also in verses 12, 16, 21, 24 and 25.
n.7: Hebrew *iwwelet*, "folly", the word related to *ewil*, "fool" (see 1:7).
n.8: Hebrew *rasha*: one who is guilty of wrong (see 2:22).
n.9: Hebrew *tsaddiq*: one who does what is right (see 2:20).
n.10: Literally "and there is no heart". In Hebrew thought the heart is the seat of understanding.
n.11: Literally "lacks heart".
n.12: That is, guarantees his neighbor's debt (see 6:1–5). Literally "before his neighbor".
n.13: *Makes his doorway high* may be a picture of arrogance or of a showy house; some take *doorway* to mean the mouth.
n.14: Hebrew *gehah*, a word found only here, probably "healing".
n.15: Literally "from the bosom", from the fold of a garment.
n.17: The Hebrew text is written "and cool of spirit" but read "precious (that is, restrained) of spirit".
n.18: Hebrew *tevunah* (see 2:2).
n.19: Hebrew *ewil*, the morally perverse, stubborn fool (see 1:7).

v: Whoever isolates himself seeks his own desire; he bursts out against all sound wisdom.[^1]
לְֽ֭תַאֲוָה יְבַקֵּ֣שׁ נִפְרָ֑ד בְּכָל־תּ֝וּשִׁיָּ֗ה יִתְגַּלָּֽע׃
A fool[^2] takes no pleasure in insight,[^3] but only in displaying his own mind.
לֹֽא־יַחְפֹּ֣ץ כְּ֭סִיל בִּתְבוּנָ֑ה כִּ֝֗י אִֽם־בְּהִתְגַּלּ֥וֹת לִבּֽוֹ׃
When the wicked[^4] comes, contempt comes too, and with dishonor comes disgrace.
בְּֽבוֹא־רָ֭שָׁע בָּ֣א גַם־בּ֑וּז וְֽעִם־קָל֥וֹן חֶרְפָּֽה׃
The words of a person's mouth are deep waters; the fountain of wisdom is a flowing stream.
מַ֣יִם עֲ֭מֻקִּים דִּבְרֵ֣י פִי־אִ֑ישׁ נַ֥חַל נֹ֝בֵ֗עַ מְק֣וֹר חָכְמָֽה׃
It is not good to show favor to the wicked,[^5] or to deprive the righteous[^6] of justice.
שְׂאֵ֣ת פְּנֵי־רָשָׁ֣ע לֹא־ט֑וֹב לְהַטּ֥וֹת צַ֝דִּ֗יק בַּמִּשְׁפָּֽט׃
A fool's lips walk into a quarrel, and his mouth invites a beating.
שִׂפְתֵ֣י כְ֭סִיל יָבֹ֣אֽוּ בְרִ֑יב וּ֝פִ֗יו לְֽמַהֲלֻמ֥וֹת יִקְרָֽא׃
A fool's mouth is his ruin, and his lips are a snare for his life.
פִּֽי־כְ֭סִיל מְחִתָּה־ל֑וֹ וּ֝שְׂפָתָ֗יו מוֹקֵ֥שׁ נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃
The words of a gossip are like tasty morsels;[^7] they go down into the inner parts of the body.
דִּבְרֵ֣י נִ֭רְגָּן כְּמִֽתְלַהֲמִ֑ים וְ֝הֵ֗ם יָרְד֥וּ חַדְרֵי־בָֽטֶן׃
Whoever is slack in his work is brother to one who destroys.
גַּ֭ם מִתְרַפֶּ֣ה בִמְלַאכְתּ֑וֹ אָ֥ח ה֝֗וּא לְבַ֣עַל מַשְׁחִֽית׃
The name of the LORD[^8] is a strong tower; the righteous run into it and are safe.
מִגְדַּל־עֹ֭ז שֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֑ה בּֽוֹ־יָר֖וּץ צַדִּ֣יק וְנִשְׂגָּֽב׃
The wealth of the rich is their strong city; in their imagination[^9] it is like a high wall.
ה֣וֹן עָ֭שִׁיר קִרְיַ֣ת עֻזּ֑וֹ וּכְחוֹמָ֥ה נִ֝שְׂגָּבָ֗ה בְּמַשְׂכִּיתֽוֹ׃
Before destruction a person's heart is proud, but humility comes before honor.
לִפְנֵי־שֶׁ֭בֶר יִגְבַּ֣הּ לֵ[t]ב־אִ֑ישׁ וְלִפְנֵ֖י כָב֣וֹד עֲנָוֽ͏ָה׃
Whoever answers before he listens, it is folly[^10] and shame to him.
מֵשִׁ֣יב דָּ֭בָר בְּטֶ֣רֶם יִשְׁמָ֑ע אִוֶּ֥לֶת הִיא־ל֝֗וֹ וּכְלִמָּֽה׃
A person's spirit can endure sickness, but a crushed spirit, who can bear it?
רֽוּחַ־אִ֭ישׁ יְכַלְכֵּ֣ל מַחֲלֵ֑הוּ וְר֥וּחַ נְ֝כֵאָ֗ה מִ֣י יִשָּׂאֶֽנָּה׃
The heart of the discerning acquires knowledge, and the ear of the wise seeks knowledge.
לֵ֣ב נָ֭בוֹן יִקְנֶה־דָּ֑עַת וְאֹ֥זֶן חֲ֝כָמִ֗ים תְּבַקֶּשׁ־דָּֽעַת׃
A gift opens the way for the giver[^11] and brings him before the great.
מַתָּ֣ן אָ֭דָם יַרְחִ֣יב ל֑וֹ וְלִפְנֵ֖י גְדֹלִ֣ים יַנְחֶֽנּוּ׃
The first to state his case seems right, until the other comes and questions him.
צַדִּ֣יק הָרִאשׁ֣וֹן בְּרִיב֑וֹ *יבא־**וּבָֽא־רֵ֝עֵ֗הוּ וַחֲקָרֽוֹ׃
Casting the lot puts an end to disputes and decides between powerful opponents.
מִ֭דְיָנִים יַשְׁבִּ֣ית הַגּוֹרָ֑ל וּבֵ֖ין עֲצוּמִ֣ים יַפְרִֽיד׃
An offended brother is harder to win than a strong city,[^12] and quarrels are like the bars of a fortress.
אָ֗ח נִפְשָׁ֥ע מִקִּרְיַת־עֹ֑ז *ומדונים **וּ֝מִדְיָנִ֗ים כִּבְרִ֥יחַ אַרְמֽוֹן׃
From the fruit of a person's mouth his stomach is filled; he is satisfied with the yield of his lips.
מִפְּרִ֣י פִי־אִ֭ישׁ תִּשְׂבַּ֣ע בִּטְנ֑וֹ תְּבוּאַ֖ת שְׂפָתָ֣יו יִשְׂבָּֽע׃
Death and life are in the power of the tongue, and those who love it will eat its fruit.
מָ֣וֶת וְ֭חַיִּים בְּיַד־לָשׁ֑וֹן וְ֝אֹהֲבֶ֗יהָ יֹאכַ֥ל פִּרְיָֽהּ׃
He who finds a wife finds a good thing and obtains favor from the LORD.[^13]
מָצָ֣א אִ֭שָּׁה מָ֣צָא ט֑וֹב וַיָּ֥פֶק רָ֝צ֗וֹן מֵיְהוָֽה׃
The poor speak with pleading, but the rich answer harshly.
תַּחֲנוּנִ֥ים יְדַבֶּר־רָ֑שׁ וְ֝עָשִׁ֗יר יַעֲנֶ֥ה עַזּֽוֹת׃
A man of many companions may come to ruin,[^14] but there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother.
אִ֣ישׁ רֵ֭עִים לְהִתְרֹעֵ֑עַ וְיֵ֥שׁ אֹ֝הֵ֗ב דָּבֵ֥ק מֵאָֽח׃

n.1: Hebrew *tushiyyah*, as in 2:7. The verb *bursts out* is used of quarrels in 17:14 and 20:3.
n.2: Hebrew *kesil* (see 1:22). Also in verses 6 and 7.
n.3: Hebrew *tevunah* (see 2:2).
n.4: Hebrew *rasha*: one who is guilty of wrong (see 2:22).
n.5: Literally "to lift up the face of the wicked".
n.6: Hebrew *tsaddiq*: one who does what is right (see 2:20).
n.7: Hebrew *mitlahamim*, a rare word, probably "tasty morsels" swallowed greedily. The verse is repeated in 26:22.
n.8: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.9: Or "in their own conceit". Compare verse 10.
n.10: Hebrew *iwwelet*, "folly", the word related to *ewil*, "fool" (see 1:7).
n.11: Literally "A person's gift makes room for him".
n.12: The Hebrew of this line is difficult. Literally "A brother offended, than a strong city". The Septuagint reads "A brother helped by a brother is like a strong and high city".
n.13: The Septuagint reads "a good wife".
n.14: Or "A man of many friends has them only for company". The verb may come from a root meaning "be broken" or from one meaning "keep company".

v: Better a poor person who walks in integrity than one with crooked lips who is a fool.[^1]
טֽוֹב־רָ֭שׁ הוֹלֵ֣ךְ בְּתֻמּ֑וֹ מֵעִקֵּ֥שׁ שְׂ֝פָתָ֗יו וְה֣וּא כְסִֽיל׃
Desire without knowledge is not good, and whoever hurries with his feet sins.[^2]
גַּ֤ם בְּלֹא־דַ֣עַת נֶ֣פֶשׁ לֹא־ט֑וֹב וְאָ֖ץ בְּרַגְלַ֣יִם חוֹטֵֽא׃
A person's folly[^3] ruins his way, but his heart rages against the LORD.[^4]
אִוֶּ֣לֶת אָ֭דָם תְּסַלֵּ֣ף דַּרְכּ֑וֹ וְעַל־יְ֝הוָ֗ה יִזְעַ֥ף לִבּֽוֹ׃
Wealth adds many friends, but the poor is separated from his friend.
ה֗וֹן יֹ֭סִיף רֵעִ֣ים רַבִּ֑ים וְ֝דָ֗ל מֵרֵ֥עהוּ יִפָּרֵֽד׃
A false witness will not go unpunished, and one who breathes out lies will not escape.
עֵ֣ד שְׁ֭קָרִים לֹ֣א יִנָּקֶ֑ה וְיָפִ֥יחַ כְּ֝זָבִ֗ים לֹ֣א יִמָּלֵֽט׃
Many seek the favor of a generous person, and everyone is a friend to one who gives gifts.
רַ֭בִּים יְחַלּ֣וּ פְנֵֽי־נָדִ֑יב וְכָל־הָ֝רֵ֗עַ לְאִ֣ישׁ מַתָּֽן׃
All the brothers of a poor person hate him; how much more do his friends keep far from him! He pursues them with words, but words are all he has.[^5]
כָּֽ[m]ל אֲחֵי־רָ֨שׁ ׀ שְֽׂנֵאֻ֗הוּ אַ֤ף כִּ֣י מְ֭רֵעֵהוּ רָחֲק֣וּ מִמֶּ֑נּוּ מְרַדֵּ֖ף אֲמָרִ֣ים *לא־**לוֹ־הֵֽמָּה׃
Whoever gains sense[^6] loves himself; whoever keeps insight[^7] will find good.
קֹֽנֶה־לֵּ֭ב אֹהֵ֣ב נַפְשׁ֑וֹ שֹׁמֵ֥ר תְּ֝בוּנָ֗ה לִמְצֹא־טֽוֹב׃
A false witness will not go unpunished, and one who breathes out lies will perish.
עֵ֣ד שְׁ֭קָרִים לֹ֣א יִנָּקֶ֑ה וְיָפִ֖יחַ כְּזָבִ֣ים יֹאבֵֽד׃ פ
Luxury is not fitting for a fool, still less for a servant to rule over princes.
לֹֽא־נָאוֶ֣ה לִכְסִ֣יל תַּעֲנ֑וּג אַ֝ף כִּֽי־לְעֶ֤בֶד ׀ מְשֹׁ֬ל בְּשָׂרִֽים׃
A person's good sense[^8] makes him slow to anger, and it is his glory to overlook an offense.
שֵׂ֣כֶל אָ֭דָם הֶאֱרִ֣יךְ אַפּ֑וֹ וְ֝תִפאַרְתּ֗וֹ עֲבֹ֣ר עַל־פָּֽשַׁע׃
A king's rage is like the roar of a lion, but his favor is like dew on the grass.
נַ֣הַם כַּ֭כְּפִיר זַ֣עַף מֶ֑לֶךְ וּכְטַ֖ל עַל־עֵ֣שֶׂב רְצוֹנֽוֹ׃
A foolish son is ruin to his father, and a wife's quarrels are a constant dripping.[^9]
הַוֺּ֣ת לְ֭אָבִיו בֵּ֣ן כְּסִ֑יל וְדֶ֥לֶף טֹ֝רֵ֗ד מִדְיְנֵ֥י אִשָּֽׁה׃
House and wealth are an inheritance from fathers, but a sensible wife[^10] is from the LORD.
בַּ֣יִת וָ֭הוֹן נַחֲלַ֣ת אָב֑וֹת וּ֝מֵיְהוָ֗ה אִשָּׁ֥ה מַשְׂכָּֽלֶת׃
Laziness casts into a deep sleep, and an idle person will go hungry.
עַ֭צְלָה תַּפִּ֣יל תַּרְדֵּמָ֑ה וְנֶ֖פֶשׁ רְמִיָּ֣ה תִרְעָֽב׃
Whoever keeps the command keeps his life; whoever is careless of his ways will die.[^11]
שֹׁמֵ֣ר מִ֭צְוָה שֹׁמֵ֣ר נַפְשׁ֑וֹ בּוֹזֵ֖ה דְרָכָ֣יו *יומת **יָמֽוּת׃
Whoever is kind to the poor lends to the LORD, and he will repay him for his deed.
מַלְוֵ֣ה יְ֭הוָה ח֣וֹנֵֽן דָּ֑ל וּ֝גְמֻל֗וֹ יְשַׁלֶּם־לֽוֹ׃
Discipline your son while there is hope; do not set your heart on his death.[^12]
יַסֵּ֣ר בִּ֭נְךָ כִּי־יֵ֣שׁ תִּקְוָ֑ה וְאֶל־הֲ֝מִית֗וֹ אַל־תִּשָּׂ֥א נַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃
A person of great anger[^13] must pay the penalty; if you rescue him, you will have to do it again.
*גרל־**גְּֽדָל־חֵ֭מָה נֹ֣שֵׂא עֹ֑נֶשׁ כִּ֥י אִם־תַּ֝צִּ֗יל וְע֣וֹד תּוֹסִֽף׃
Listen to advice and accept discipline,[^14] so that you may be wise in the end.
שְׁמַ֣ע עֵ֭צָה וְקַבֵּ֣ל מוּסָ֑ר לְ֝מַ֗עַן תֶּחְכַּ֥ם בְּאַחֲרִיתֶֽךָ׃
Many plans are in a person's heart, but it is the purpose of the LORD that will stand.
רַבּ֣וֹת מַחֲשָׁב֣וֹת בְּלֶב־אִ֑ישׁ וַעֲצַ֥ת יְ֝הוָ֗ה הִ֣יא תָקֽוּם׃
What is desired in a person is faithful love,[^15] and it is better to be poor than a liar.
תַּאֲוַ֣ת אָדָ֣ם חַסְדּ֑וֹ וְטֽוֹב־רָ֝שׁ מֵאִ֥ישׁ כָּזָֽב׃
The fear of the LORD leads to life; whoever has it rests content, untouched by harm.
יִרְאַ֣ת יְהוָ֣ה לְחַיִּ֑ים וְשָׂבֵ֥עַ יָ֝לִ֗ין בַּל־יִפָּ֥קֶד רָֽע׃
The lazy person[^16] buries his hand in the dish; he will not even bring it back to his mouth.
טָ֘מַ֤ן עָצֵ֣ל יָ֭דוֹ בַּצַּלָּ֑חַת גַּם־אֶל־פִּ֝֗יהוּ לֹ֣א יְשִׁיבֶֽנָּה׃
Strike a mocker,[^17] and the simple[^18] will learn prudence;[^19] correct a discerning person, and he will gain knowledge.
לֵ֣ץ תַּ֭כֶּה וּפֶ֣תִי יַעְרִ֑ם וְהוֹכִ֥יחַ לְ֝נָב֗וֹן יָבִ֥ין דָּֽעַת׃
Whoever robs his father and drives out his mother is a son who brings shame and disgrace.
מְֽשַׁדֶּד־אָ֭ב יַבְרִ֣יחַ אֵ֑ם בֵּ֝֗ן מֵבִ֥ישׁ וּמַחְפִּֽיר׃
Stop listening to discipline, my son, and you will stray from the words of knowledge.
חַֽדַל־בְּ֭נִי לִשְׁמֹ֣עַ מוּסָ֑ר לִ֝שְׁג֗וֹת מֵֽאִמְרֵי־דָֽעַת׃
A worthless witness[^20] mocks at justice, and the mouth of the wicked[^21] swallows iniquity.
עֵ֣ד בְּ֭לִיַּעַל יָלִ֣יץ מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וּפִ֥י רְ֝שָׁעִ֗ים יְבַלַּע־אָֽוֶן׃
Punishments are ready for mockers, and beatings for the backs of fools.
נָכ֣וֹנוּ לַלֵּצִ֣ים שְׁפָטִ֑ים וּ֝מַהֲלֻמ֗וֹת לְגֵ֣ו כְסִילִֽים׃

n.1: Hebrew *kesil* (see 1:22). Also in verses 10, 13 and 29. Compare 28:6.
n.2: Or "misses the way". The verb *chata* means both "sin" and "miss" (8:36).
n.3: Hebrew *iwwelet*, "folly", the word related to *ewil*, "fool" (see 1:7).
n.4: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.5: The Hebrew of this line is difficult. The text is written *lo*, "not", but read *lo*, "to him": literally "pursuing words, they are his". On the written form the line means "he pursues them with words, but they are gone". The verse has three lines instead of two, and the Septuagint has a different and longer text.
n.6: Literally "gains heart".
n.7: Hebrew *tevunah* (see 2:2).
n.8: Hebrew *sekhel*, "good sense, insight".
n.9: That is, the dripping of a leaking roof (27:15).
n.10: Hebrew *ishah maskalet*, a wife who acts with good sense (compare *maskil*, 10:5).
n.11: The Hebrew text is written "will be put to death" but read "will die". *Is careless of his ways* is literally "despises his ways".
n.12: Literally "and to his death do not lift up your soul". This may mean "do not be a party to his ruin" by neglecting discipline, or "do not let your anger go so far as to kill him".
n.13: The Hebrew text is written with a word of unclear meaning, perhaps "rough", but read "great".
n.14: Hebrew *musar*: discipline, training and correction (see 1:2). Also in verse 27.
n.15: Hebrew *chesed*. Or, taking *chesed* as in 14:34, "A person's greed is his disgrace".
n.16: Hebrew *atsel*, traditionally "sluggard" (see 6:6). The verse is repeated in 26:15.
n.17: Hebrew *lets*: one who scorns wisdom and laughs at correction (see 1:22). Also in verse 29.
n.18: Hebrew *peti*: a naive, inexperienced person, easily led (see 1:4).
n.19: Hebrew *ya'rim*, from the same root as *ormah*, "prudence" (see 1:4).
n.21: Hebrew *resha'im*, plural of *rasha*: those who are guilty of wrong (see 2:22).

v: Wine is a mocker,[^1] beer a brawler, and whoever is led astray by it is not wise.
לֵ֣ץ הַ֭יַּ[t]ין הֹמֶ֣ה שֵׁכָ֑ר וְכָל־שֹׁ֥גֶה בּ֝֗וֹ לֹ֣א יֶחְכָּֽם׃
The terror of a king is like the roar of a lion; whoever provokes him forfeits his life.
נַ֣הַם כַּ֭כְּפִיר אֵ֣ימַת מֶ֑לֶךְ מִ֝תְעַבְּר֗וֹ חוֹטֵ֥א נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃
It is an honor for a person to keep away from strife, but every fool[^2] bursts into quarrels.
כָּב֣וֹד לָ֭אִישׁ שֶׁ֣בֶת מֵרִ֑יב וְכָל־אֱ֝וִ֗יל יִתְגַּלָּֽע׃
The lazy person[^3] does not plow in autumn; at harvest he looks for a crop, and there is nothing.
מֵ֭חֹרֶף עָצֵ֣ל לֹא־יַחֲרֹ֑שׁ *ישאל **וְשָׁאַ֖ל בַּקָּצִ֣יר וָאָֽיִן׃
The purpose in a person's heart is deep water, but a person of insight[^4] draws it out.
מַ֣יִם עֲ֭מֻקִּים עֵצָ֣ה בְלֶב־אִ֑ישׁ וְאִ֖ישׁ תְּבוּנָ֣ה יִדְלֶֽנָּה׃
Many a person proclaims his own loyalty,[^5] but a faithful person, who can find?
רָב־אָדָ֗ם יִ֭קְרָא אִ֣ישׁ חַסְדּ֑וֹ וְאִ֥ישׁ אֱ֝מוּנִ֗ים מִ֣י יִמְצָֽא׃
The righteous[^6] walks in his integrity; happy[^7] are his children after him.
מִתְהַלֵּ֣ךְ בְּתֻמּ֣וֹ צַדִּ֑יק אַשְׁרֵ֖י בָנָ֣יו אַחֲרָֽיו׃
A king who sits on the throne of judgment winnows out all evil with his eyes.
מֶ֗לֶךְ יוֹשֵׁ֥ב עַל־כִּסֵּא־דִ֑ין מְזָרֶ֖ה בְעֵינָ֣יו כָּל־רָֽע׃
Who can say, "I have made my heart clean; I am pure from my sin"?
מִֽי־יֹ֭אמַר זִכִּ֣יתִי לִבִּ֑י טָ֝הַ֗רְתִּי מֵחַטָּאתִֽי׃
Two different weights and two different measures,[^8] both are detestable to the LORD.[^9]
אֶ֣בֶן וָ֭אֶבֶן אֵיפָ֣ה וְאֵיפָ֑ה תּוֹעֲבַ֥ת יְ֝הוָ֗ה גַּם־שְׁנֵיהֶֽם׃
Even a child makes himself known by his actions,[^10] whether his conduct is pure and right.
גַּ֣ם בְּ֭מַעֲלָלָיו יִתְנַכֶּר־נָ֑עַר אִם־זַ֖ךְ וְאִם־יָשָׁ֣ר פָּעֳלֽוֹ׃
The ear that hears and the eye that sees, the LORD has made them both.
אֹ֣זֶן שֹׁ֭מַעַת וְעַ֣יִן רֹאָ֑ה יְ֝הוָ֗ה עָשָׂ֥ה גַם־שְׁנֵיהֶֽם׃
Do not love sleep, or you will become poor; open your eyes, and you will have plenty of bread.
אַל־תֶּֽאֱהַ֣ב שֵׁ֭נָה פֶּן־תִּוָּרֵ֑שׁ פְּקַ֖ח עֵינֶ֣יךָ שְֽׂבַֽע־לָֽחֶם׃
"Bad, bad," says the buyer; but when he goes on his way, then he boasts.
רַ֣ע רַ֭ע יֹאמַ֣ר הַקּוֹנֶ֑ה וְאֹזֵ֥ל ל֝֗וֹ אָ֣ז יִתְהַלָּֽל׃
There is gold and plenty of coral,[^11] but lips of knowledge are a precious jewel.
יֵ֣שׁ זָ֭הָב וְרָב־פְּנִינִ֑ים וּכְלִ֥י יְ֝קָ֗ר שִׂפְתֵי־דָֽעַת׃
Take the garment of one who puts up security for a stranger; hold it in pledge for a foreign woman.[^12]
לְֽקַח־בִּ֭גְדוֹ כִּי־עָ֣רַב זָ֑ר וּבְעַ֖ד *נכרים **נָכְרִיָּ֣ה חַבְלֵֽהוּ׃
Bread gained by deceit is sweet to a person, but afterward his mouth will be full of gravel.
עָרֵ֣ב לָ֭אִישׁ לֶ֣חֶם שָׁ֑קֶר וְ֝אַחַ֗ר יִמָּֽלֵא־פִ֥יהוּ חָצָֽץ׃
Plans are established by advice; wage war with guidance.[^13]
מַ֭חֲשָׁבוֹת בְּעֵצָ֣ה תִכּ֑וֹן וּ֝בְתַחְבֻּל֗וֹת עֲשֵׂ֣ה מִלְחָמָֽה׃
Whoever goes about as a gossip reveals secrets, so do not associate with one who talks too much.
גּֽוֹלֶה־סּ֭וֹד הוֹלֵ֣ךְ רָכִ֑יל וּלְפֹתֶ֥ה שְׂ֝פָתָ֗יו לֹ֣א תִתְעָרָֽב׃
Whoever curses his father or his mother, his lamp will go out in the blackest darkness.
מְ֭קַלֵּל אָבִ֣יו וְאִמּ֑וֹ יִֽדְעַ֥ךְ נֵ֝ר֗וֹ *באישון **בֶּאֱשׁ֥וּן חֹֽשֶׁךְ׃
An inheritance gained in haste at the beginning[^14] will not be blessed in the end.
נַ֭חֲלָה *מבחלת **מְבֹהֶ֣לֶת בָּרִאשֹׁנָ֑ה וְ֝אַחֲרִיתָ֗הּ לֹ֣א תְבֹרָֽךְ׃
Do not say, "I will pay back evil!" Wait for the LORD, and he will rescue you.
אַל־תֹּאמַ֥ר אֲשַׁלְּמָה־רָ֑ע קַוֵּ֥ה לַֽ֝יהוָ֗ה וְיֹ֣שַֽׁע לָֽךְ׃
Two different weights are detestable to the LORD, and dishonest scales are not good.
תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה אֶ֣בֶן וָאָ֑בֶן וּמֹאזְנֵ֖י מִרְמָ֣ה לֹא־טֽוֹב׃
A man's steps are from the LORD; how then can anyone understand his own way?
מֵיהוָ֥ה מִצְעֲדֵי־גָ֑בֶר וְ֝אָדָ֗ם מַה־יָּבִ֥ין דַּרְכּֽוֹ׃
It is a trap for a person to say rashly, "It is holy!"[^15] and only afterward to think about his vows.
מוֹקֵ֣שׁ אָ֭דָם יָ֣לַע קֹ֑דֶשׁ וְאַחַ֖ר נְדָרִ֣ים לְבַקֵּֽר׃
A wise king winnows out the wicked[^16] and drives the wheel over them.[^17]
מְזָרֶ֣ה רְ֭שָׁעִים מֶ֣לֶךְ חָכָ֑ם וַיָּ֖שֶׁב עֲלֵיהֶ֣ם אוֹפָֽן׃
The human spirit[^18] is the lamp of the LORD, searching all the inner parts of the body.
נֵ֣ר יְ֭הוָה נִשְׁמַ֣ת אָדָ֑ם חֹ֝פֵ֗שׂ כָּל־חַדְרֵי־בָֽטֶן׃
Faithful love and truth[^19] guard a king; by faithful love his throne is upheld.
חֶ֣סֶד וֶ֭אֱמֶת יִצְּרוּ־מֶ֑לֶךְ וְסָעַ֖ד בַּחֶ֣סֶד כִּסְאֽוֹ׃
The glory of young men is their strength, and the splendor of the old is their gray hair.
תִּפְאֶ֣רֶת בַּחוּרִ֣ים כֹּחָ֑ם וַהֲדַ֖ר זְקֵנִ֣ים שֵׂיבָֽה׃
Blows that wound scour away evil, and beatings, the inner parts of the body.[^20]
חַבֻּר֣וֹת פֶּ֭צַע *תמריק **תַּמְר֣וּק בְּרָ֑ע וּ֝מַכּ֗וֹת חַדְרֵי־בָֽטֶן׃

n.1: Hebrew *lets*, the word used for the person who scorns wisdom (see 1:22).
n.2: Hebrew *ewil*, the morally perverse, stubborn fool (see 1:7).
n.3: Hebrew *atsel*, traditionally "sluggard" (see 6:6).
n.4: Hebrew *tevunah* (see 2:2).
n.5: Hebrew *chesed*, "faithful love".
n.6: Hebrew *tsaddiq*: one who does what is right (see 2:20).
n.7: Hebrew *ashrei*: happy, fortunate; traditionally "blessed".
n.8: Literally "a stone and a stone, an ephah and an ephah", one for buying and one for selling. Hebrew *ephah*, a measure for grain, used here for any measure of volume. Compare Deuteronomy 25:13–15.
n.9: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.10: Or "Even a child may disguise himself by his actions".
n.11: Hebrew *peninim*, as in 3:15.
n.12: The Hebrew text is written "for foreigners" but read "for a foreign woman". Compare 27:13.
n.13: Hebrew *tachbulot*, as in 1:5.
n.14: The Hebrew text is written with a different word, perhaps "gained greedily", but read "gained in haste".
n.15: That is, to dedicate something to God without thinking.
n.16: Hebrew *resha'im*, plural of *rasha*: those who are guilty of wrong (see 2:22).
n.17: The wheel of a threshing cart, used to separate grain from straw (Isaiah 28:27–28).
n.18: Literally "The breath (*neshamah*) of a human being" (Genesis 2:7).
n.19: Hebrew *chesed ve-emet*: faithful love and reliability (see 3:3).
n.20: Literally "and blows, the chambers of the belly". The verb of the first line is understood again here.

v: The king's heart is like streams of water in the hand of the LORD;[^1] he turns it wherever he wishes.
פַּלְגֵי־מַ֣יִם לֶב־מֶ֭לֶךְ בְּיַד־יְהוָ֑ה עַֽל־כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֖ר יַחְפֹּ֣ץ יַטֶּֽנּוּ׃
All a person's ways seem right in his own eyes, but the LORD weighs hearts.
כָּֽל־דֶּרֶךְ־אִ֭ישׁ יָשָׁ֣ר בְּעֵינָ֑יו וְתֹכֵ֖ן לִבּ֣וֹת יְהוָֽה׃
Doing righteousness and justice is more acceptable to the LORD than sacrifice.
עֲ֭שֹׂה צְדָקָ֣ה וּמִשְׁפָּ֑ט נִבְחָ֖ר לַיהוָ֣ה מִזָּֽבַח׃
Haughty eyes and a proud heart, the lamp[^2] of the wicked,[^3] are sin.
רוּם־עֵ֭ינַיִם וּרְחַב־לֵ֑ב נִ֖ר רְשָׁעִ֣ים חַטָּֽאת׃
The plans of the diligent lead only to profit, but everyone who is hasty comes only to need.
מַחְשְׁב֣וֹת חָ֭רוּץ אַךְ־לְמוֹתָ֑ר וְכָל־אָ֝֗ץ אַךְ־לְמַחְסֽוֹר׃
Getting treasures by a lying tongue is a vapor[^4] blown away, for those who seek death.[^5]
פֹּ֣עַל א֭וֹצָרוֹת בִּלְשׁ֣וֹן שָׁ֑קֶר הֶ֥בֶל נִ֝דָּ֗ף מְבַקְשֵׁי־מָֽוֶת׃
The violence of the wicked will sweep them away, because they refuse to do what is just.
שֹׁד־רְשָׁעִ֥ים יְגוֹרֵ֑ם כִּ֥י מֵ֝אֲנ֗וּ לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת מִשְׁפָּֽט׃
The way of a guilty person[^6] is crooked, but the conduct of the pure is upright.
הֲפַכְפַּ֬ךְ דֶּ֣רֶךְ אִ֣ישׁ וָזָ֑ר וְ֝זַ֗ךְ יָשָׁ֥ר פָּעֳלֽוֹ׃
Better to live in a corner of the roof than in a house shared with a quarrelsome wife.
ט֗וֹב לָשֶׁ֥בֶת עַל־פִּנַּת־גָּ֑ג מֵאֵ֥שֶׁת מִ֝דְיָנִ֗ים וּבֵ֥ית חָֽבֶר׃
The soul of the wicked craves evil; his neighbor finds no mercy in his eyes.
נֶ֣פֶשׁ רָ֭שָׁע אִוְּתָה־רָ֑ע לֹא־יֻחַ֖ן בְּעֵינָ֣יו רֵעֵֽהוּ׃
When a mocker[^7] is punished, the simple[^8] becomes wise; when a wise person is instructed, he gains knowledge.
בַּעְנָשׁ־לֵ֭ץ יֶחְכַּם־פֶּ֑תִי וּבְהַשְׂכִּ֥יל לְ֝חָכָ֗ם יִקַּח־דָּֽעַת׃
The Righteous One[^9] observes the house of the wicked; he throws the wicked down to ruin.
מַשְׂכִּ֣יל צַ֭דִּיק לְבֵ֣ית רָשָׁ֑ע מְסַלֵּ֖ף רְשָׁעִ֣ים לָרָֽע׃
Whoever shuts his ears to the cry of the poor will himself call out and not be answered.
אֹטֵ֣ם אָ֭זְנוֹ מִזַּעֲקַת־דָּ֑ל גַּֽם־ה֥וּא יִ֝קְרָ֗א וְלֹ֣א יֵעָנֶֽה׃
A gift given in secret calms anger, and a bribe in the fold of the cloak calms fierce wrath.
מַתָּ֣ן בַּ֭סֵּתֶר יִכְפֶּה־אָ֑ף וְשֹׁ֥חַד בַּ֝חֵ֗ק חֵמָ֥ה עַזָּֽה׃
When justice is done, it is a joy to the righteous but terror to evildoers.
שִׂמְחָ֣ה לַ֭צַּדִּיק עֲשׂ֣וֹת מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וּ֝מְחִתָּ֗ה לְפֹ֣עֲלֵי אָֽוֶן׃
Whoever wanders from the way of good sense will rest in the assembly of the dead.[^10]
אָדָ֗ם תּ֖[d]וֹעֶה מִדֶּ֣רֶךְ הַשְׂכֵּ֑ל בִּקְהַ֖ל רְפָאִ֣ים יָנֽוּחַ׃
Whoever loves pleasure will be poor; whoever loves wine and oil will not grow rich.
אִ֣ישׁ מַ֭חְסוֹר אֹהֵ֣ב שִׂמְחָ֑ה אֹהֵ֥ב יַֽיִן־וָ֝שֶׁ֗מֶן לֹ֣א יַעֲשִֽׁיר׃
The wicked is a ransom for the righteous, and the treacherous takes the place of the upright.
כֹּ֣פֶר לַצַּדִּ֣יק רָשָׁ֑ע וְתַ֖חַת יְשָׁרִ֣ים בּוֹגֵֽד׃
Better to live in a desert land than with a quarrelsome and angry wife.
ט֗וֹב שֶׁ֥בֶת בְּאֶֽרֶץ־מִדְבָּ֑ר מֵאֵ֖שֶׁת *מדונים **מִדְיָנִ֣ים וָכָֽעַס׃
Precious treasure and oil are in the dwelling of the wise, but a foolish person[^11] swallows it up.
אוֹצָ֤ר ׀ נֶחְמָ֣ד וָ֭שֶׁמֶן בִּנְוֵ֣ה חָכָ֑ם וּכְסִ֖יל אָדָ֣ם יְבַלְּעֶֽנּוּ׃
Whoever pursues righteousness and faithful love will find life, righteousness[^12] and honor.
רֹ֭דֵף צְדָקָ֣ה וָחָ֑סֶד יִמְצָ֥א חַ֝יִּ֗ים צְדָקָ֥ה וְכָבֽוֹד׃
A wise person climbs the city of the mighty and brings down the stronghold they trusted in.
עִ֣יר גִּ֭בֹּרִים עָלָ֣ה חָכָ֑ם וַ֝יֹּ֗רֶד עֹ֣ז מִבְטֶחָֽה׃
Whoever guards his mouth and his tongue guards his life from troubles.
שֹׁמֵ֣ר פִּ֭יו וּלְשׁוֹנ֑וֹ שֹׁמֵ֖ר מִצָּר֣וֹת נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃
The proud and arrogant person, "Mocker" is his name; he acts with insolent fury.
זֵ֣ד יָ֭הִיר לֵ֣ץ שְׁמ֑וֹ ע֝וֹשֶׂ֗ה בְּעֶבְרַ֥ת זָדֽוֹן׃
The craving of the lazy person[^13] kills him, for his hands refuse to work.
תַּאֲוַ֣ת עָצֵ֣ל תְּמִיתֶ֑נּוּ כִּֽי־מֵאֲנ֖וּ יָדָ֣יו לַעֲשֽׂוֹת׃
All day long he craves and craves,[^14] but the righteous gives and does not hold back.
כָּל־הַ֭יּוֹם הִתְאַוָּ֣ה תַאֲוָ֑ה וְצַדִּ֥יק יִ֝תֵּ֗ן וְלֹ֣א יַחְשֹֽׂךְ׃
The sacrifice of the wicked is detestable; how much more when he brings it with evil intent!
זֶ֣בַח רְ֭שָׁעִים תּוֹעֵבָ֑ה אַ֝֗ף כִּֽי־בְזִמָּ֥ה יְבִיאֶֽנּוּ׃
A false witness will perish, but one who listens will speak forever.[^15]
עֵד־כְּזָבִ֥ים יֹאבֵ֑ד וְאִ֥ישׁ שׁ֝וֹמֵ֗עַ לָנֶ֥צַח יְדַבֵּֽר׃
A wicked man puts on a bold face, but the upright gives thought to his way.[^16]
הֵעֵ֬ז אִ֣ישׁ רָשָׁ֣ע בְּפָנָ֑יו וְ֝יָשָׁ֗ר ה֤וּא ׀ *יכין **יָבִ֬ין *דרכיו **דַּרְכּֽוֹ׃
There is no wisdom, no insight,[^17] no counsel that can stand against the LORD.
אֵ֣ין חָ֭כְמָה וְאֵ֣ין תְּבוּנָ֑ה וְאֵ֥ין עֵ֝צָ֗ה לְנֶ֣גֶד יְהוָֽה׃ פ
The horse is made ready for the day of battle, but victory belongs to the LORD.
ס֗וּס מ֭וּכָן לְי֣וֹם מִלְחָמָ֑ה וְ֝לַֽיהוָ֗ה הַתְּשׁוּעָֽה׃

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.2: The Hebrew vowel points read *nir*, "newly plowed ground" (as in 13:23): "the plowing of the wicked". The same consonants can be read *ner*, "lamp" (13:9; 20:27).
n.3: Hebrew *resha'im*, plural of *rasha*: those who are guilty of wrong (see 2:22).
n.4: Hebrew *hevel*, "breath, vapor", the word used throughout Ecclesiastes.
n.5: The Septuagint and the Vulgate read "snares of death".
n.6: Hebrew *vazar*, a word found only here, probably "guilty". Or "The way of a man is crooked and strange".
n.7: Hebrew *lets*: one who scorns wisdom and laughs at correction (see 1:22). Also in verse 24.
n.8: Hebrew *peti*: a naive, inexperienced person, easily led (see 1:4).
n.9: Probably God (compare Job 34:17). Or "A righteous person observes the house of the wicked; the wicked are thrown down to ruin". Hebrew *tsaddiq* (see 2:20).
n.10: Hebrew *rephaim*, the spirits of the dead (see 2:18).
n.11: Literally "a fool (*kesil*) of a man" (see 1:22).
n.12: Or "prosperity", as in 8:18.
n.13: Hebrew *atsel*, traditionally "sluggard" (see 6:6).
n.14: Literally "he craves a craving", probably the lazy person of verse 25.
n.15: Or "will speak with lasting effect". Hebrew *lanetsach*, "forever, to the end".
n.16: The Hebrew text is written "makes his ways firm" but read "gives thought to his way".
n.17: Hebrew *tevunah* (see 2:2).

v: A good name is to be chosen rather than great riches, and favor is better than silver and gold.
נִבְחָ֣ר שֵׁ֭ם מֵעֹ֣שֶׁר רָ֑ב מִכֶּ֥סֶף וּ֝מִזָּהָ֗ב חֵ֣ן טֽוֹב׃
The rich and the poor meet together; the LORD[^1] is the maker of them all.
עָשִׁ֣יר וָרָ֣שׁ נִפְגָּ֑שׁוּ עֹשֵׂ֖ה כֻלָּ֣ם יְהוָֽה׃
The prudent[^2] sees danger and hides himself, but the simple[^3] go on and pay for it.
עָר֤וּם ׀ רָאָ֣ה רָעָ֣ה *ויסתר **וְנִסְתָּ֑ר וּ֝פְתָיִ֗ים עָבְר֥וּ וְֽנֶעֱנָֽשׁוּ׃
The reward for humility and the fear of the LORD is riches, honor and life.[^4]
עֵ֣קֶב עֲ֭נָוָה יִרְאַ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה עֹ֖שֶׁר וְכָב֣וֹד וְחַיִּֽים׃
Thorns and snares are in the way of the crooked; whoever guards his life will keep far from them.
צִנִּ֣ים פַּ֭חִים בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ עִקֵּ֑שׁ שׁוֹמֵ֥ר נַ֝פְשׁ֗וֹ יִרְחַ֥ק מֵהֶֽם׃
Train a child in the way he should go;[^5] even when he is old he will not turn away from it.
חֲנֹ֣ךְ לַ֭נַּעַר עַל־פִּ֣י דַרְכּ֑וֹ גַּ֥ם כִּֽי־יַ֝זְקִ֗ין לֹֽא־יָס֥וּר מִמֶּֽנָּה׃
The rich rules over the poor, and the borrower is servant[^6] to the lender.
עָ֭שִׁיר בְּרָשִׁ֣ים יִמְשׁ֑וֹל וְעֶ֥בֶד לֹ֝וֶ֗ה לְאִ֣ישׁ מַלְוֽ͏ֶה׃
Whoever sows injustice will reap trouble, and the rod of his fury will come to an end.[^7]
זוֹרֵ֣עַ עַ֭וְלָה *יקצו[y]*ר־**יִקְצָר־אָ֑וֶן וְשֵׁ֖בֶט עֶבְרָת֣וֹ יִכְלֶֽה׃
Whoever has a generous eye will be blessed, for he gives some of his bread to the poor.
טֽוֹב־עַ֭יִן ה֣וּא יְבֹרָ֑ךְ כִּֽי־נָתַ֖ן מִלַּחְמ֣וֹ לַדָּֽל׃
Drive out the mocker,[^8] and strife goes out; quarreling and insults will stop.
גָּ֣רֵֽשׁ לֵ֭ץ וְיֵצֵ֣א מָד֑וֹן וְ֝יִשְׁבֹּ֗ת דִּ֣ין וְקָלֽוֹן׃
Whoever loves purity of heart[^9] and whose speech is gracious will have the king as his friend.
אֹהֵ֥ב *טהור־**טְהָר־לֵ֑ב חֵ֥ן שְׂ֝פָתָ֗יו רֵעֵ֥הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ׃
The eyes of the LORD watch over knowledge, but he overturns the words of the treacherous.
עֵינֵ֣י יְ֭הוָה נָ֣צְרוּ דָ֑עַת וַ֝יְסַלֵּ֗ף דִּבְרֵ֥י בֹגֵֽד׃
The lazy person[^10] says, "There is a lion outside! I will be killed in the streets!"
אָמַ֣ר עָ֭צֵל אֲרִ֣י בַח֑וּץ בְּת֥וֹךְ רְ֝חֹב֗וֹת אֵֽרָצֵֽחַ׃
The mouth of strange women[^11] is a deep pit; whoever is cursed by the LORD will fall into it.
שׁוּחָ֣ה עֲ֭מֻקָּה פִּ֣י זָר֑וֹת זְע֥וּם יְ֝הוָ֗ה *יפול־**יִפָּל־שָֽׁם׃
Folly[^12] is bound up in the heart of a child, but the rod of discipline[^13] will drive it far from him.
אִ֭וֶּלֶת קְשׁוּרָ֣ה בְלֶב־נָ֑עַר שֵׁ֥בֶט מ֝וּסָ֗ר יַרְחִיקֶ֥נָּה מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃
Whoever oppresses the poor to increase his own wealth, or gives to the rich, comes only to need.[^14]
עֹ֣שֵֽׁק דָּ֭ל לְהַרְבּ֣וֹת ל֑וֹ נֹתֵ֥ן לְ֝עָשִׁ֗יר אַךְ־לְמַחְסֽוֹר׃
Turn your ear and listen to the words of the wise,[^15] and set your heart on my knowledge,
הַ֥ט אָזְנְךָ֗ וּ֖[d]שְׁמַע דִּבְרֵ֣י חֲכָמִ֑ים וְ֝לִבְּךָ֗ תָּשִׁ֥ית לְדַעְתִּֽי׃
for it is pleasant if you keep them within you,[^16] if all of them are ready on your lips.
כִּֽי־נָ֭עִים כִּֽי־תִשְׁמְרֵ֣ם בְּבִטְנֶ֑ךָ יִכֹּ֥נוּ יַ֝חְדָּ֗ו עַל־שְׂפָתֶֽיךָ׃
So that your trust may be in the LORD, I have taught you today, even you.
לִהְי֣וֹת בַּ֭יהוָה מִבְטַחֶ֑ךָ הוֹדַעְתִּ֖יךָ הַיּ֣וֹם אַף־אָֽתָּה׃
Have I not written for you excellent sayings[^17] of advice and knowledge,
הֲלֹ֤א כָתַ֣בְתִּי לְ֭ךָ *שלשום **שָׁלִישִׁ֑ים בְּמ֖וֹעֵצֹ֣ת וָדָֽעַת׃
to teach you what is right and true, so that you may bring back a true report to those who sent you?
לְהוֹדִֽיעֲךָ֗ קֹ֭שְׁטְ אִמְרֵ֣י אֱמֶ֑ת לְהָשִׁ֥יב אֲמָרִ֥ים אֱ֝מֶ֗ת לְשֹׁלְחֶֽיךָ׃ פ
Do not rob the poor because he is poor, and do not crush the afflicted at the gate,[^18]
אַֽל־תִּגְזָל־דָּ֭ל כִּ֣י דַל־ה֑וּא וְאַל־תְּדַכֵּ֖א עָנִ֣י בַשָּֽׁעַר׃
for the LORD will plead their case and will take the life of those who rob them.
כִּֽי־יְ֭הוָה יָרִ֣יב רִיבָ֑ם וְקָבַ֖ע אֶת־קֹבְעֵיהֶ֣ם נָֽפֶשׁ׃
Do not make friends with a hot-tempered person, and do not go about with a man given to anger,
אַל־תִּ֭תְרַע אֶת־בַּ֣עַל אָ֑ף וְאֶת־אִ֥ישׁ חֵ֝מוֹת לֹ֣א תָבֽוֹא׃
or you will learn his ways[^19] and get yourself caught in a snare.
פֶּן־תֶּאֱלַ֥ף *ארחתו **אֹֽרְחֹתָ֑יו וְלָקַחְתָּ֖ מוֹקֵ֣שׁ לְנַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃
Do not be one of those who shake hands on a pledge, who put up security for debts.
אַל־תְּהִ֥י בְתֹֽקְעֵי־כָ֑ף בַּ֝עֹרְבִ֗ים מַשָּׁאֽוֹת׃
If you have nothing with which to pay, why should your bed be taken from under you?
אִם־אֵֽין־לְךָ֥ לְשַׁלֵּ֑ם לָ֥מָּה יִקַּ֥ח מִ֝שְׁכָּבְךָ֗ מִתַּחְתֶּֽיךָ׃
Do not move the ancient boundary stone that your ancestors set up.
אַל־תַּ֭סֵּג גְּב֣וּל עוֹלָ֑ם אֲשֶׁ֖ר עָשׂ֣וּ אֲבוֹתֶֽיךָ׃
Do you see a man skilled in his work? He will serve before kings; he will not serve before obscure people.
חָזִ֡יתָ אִ֤ישׁ ׀ מָ֘הִ֤יר בִּמְלַאכְתּ֗וֹ לִֽפְנֵֽי־מְלָכִ֥ים יִתְיַצָּ֑ב בַּל־יִ֝תְיַצֵּב לִפְנֵ֥י חֲשֻׁכִּֽים׃ פ

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.2: Hebrew *arum*, "shrewd, prudent" (see 1:4). The verse is repeated in 27:12.
n.3: Hebrew *peta'im*, plural of *peti*: naive, inexperienced people, easily led (see 1:4).
n.4: Literally "The reward of humility, the fear of the LORD, riches and honor and life". Or "The reward of humility, which is the fear of the LORD, is riches …".
n.5: Literally "according to his way": the way he should go, or the way that suits him.
n.6: Or "slave".
n.7: The Septuagint adds a line, "God blesses a man who is cheerful and generous", echoed in 2 Corinthians 9:7.
n.8: Hebrew *lets*: one who scorns wisdom and laughs at correction (see 1:22).
n.9: The Hebrew text is written "the pure of heart" but read "purity of heart".
n.10: Hebrew *atsel*, traditionally "sluggard" (see 6:6).
n.11: Hebrew *zarot*, plural of *zarah*, "strange woman", a woman outside one's marriage (see 2:16).
n.12: Hebrew *iwwelet*, "folly", the word related to *ewil*, "fool" (see 1:7).
n.13: Hebrew *musar*: discipline, training and correction (see 1:2).
n.14: The Hebrew is compact. Or "Oppressing the poor may increase a person's wealth, but giving to the rich leads only to need".
n.15: A new collection begins here (22:17–24:22), "the words of the wise" (compare 24:23). Much of 22:17–23:11 closely resembles an Egyptian work, the Instruction of Amenemope, which is arranged in thirty chapters (compare verse 20).
n.17: The Hebrew text is written *shilshom*, "formerly", but read *shalishim*, a word that usually means "officers" and is traditionally taken here as "excellent things". Many scholars read *sheloshim*, "thirty (sayings)", with a small change to the Hebrew (compare the note on verse 17).
n.18: The town gate, where the court met.
n.19: The Hebrew text is written "his way" but read "his ways".

v: When you sit down to eat with a ruler, consider carefully what is before you,[^1]
כִּֽי־תֵ֭שֵׁב לִלְח֣וֹם אֶת־מוֹשֵׁ֑ל בִּ֥ין תָּ֝בִ֗ין אֶת־אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְפָנֶֽיךָ׃
and put a knife to your throat if you have a big appetite.[^2]
וְשַׂמְתָּ֣ שַׂכִּ֣ין בְּלֹעֶ֑ךָ אִם־בַּ֖עַל נֶ֣פֶשׁ אָֽתָּה׃
Do not crave his delicacies, for they are deceptive food.
אַל־תִּ֭תְאָו לְמַטְעַמּוֹתָ֑יו וְ֝ה֗וּא לֶ֣חֶם כְּזָבִֽים׃
Do not wear yourself out to get rich; stop relying on your own understanding.[^3]
אַל־תִּיגַ֥ע לְֽהַעֲשִׁ֑יר מִֽבִּינָתְךָ֥ חֲדָֽל׃
When your eyes fly to it, it is gone;[^4] for it will surely make itself wings and fly off to the sky like an eagle.
*התעוף **הֲתָ֤עִיף עֵינֶ֥יךָ בּ֗וֹ וְֽאֵ֫ינֶ֥נּוּ כִּ֤י עָשֹׂ֣ה יַעֲשֶׂה־לּ֣וֹ כְנָפַ֑יִם כְּ֝נֶ֗שֶׁר *ועיף **יָע֥וּף הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃ פ
Do not eat the bread of a stingy person,[^5] and do not crave his delicacies,
אַל־תִּלְחַ֗ם אֶת־לֶ֭חֶם רַ֣ע עָ֑יִן וְאַל־*תתאו **תִּ֝תְאָ֗יו לְמַטְעַמֹּתָֽיו׃
for he is like one who keeps count in his mind.[^6] "Eat and drink!" he says to you, but his heart is not with you.
כִּ֤י ׀ כְּמּֽ[m]וֹ שָׁעַ֥ר בְּנַפְשׁ֗וֹ כֶּ֫ן־ה֥וּא אֱכֹ֣ל וּ֭שְׁתֵה יֹ֣אמַר לָ֑ךְ וְ֝לִבּ֗וֹ בַּל־עִמָּֽךְ׃
You will vomit up the morsel you have eaten and waste your pleasant words.
פִּֽתְּךָ־אָכַ֥לְתָּ תְקִיאֶ֑נָּה וְ֝שִׁחַ֗תָּ דְּבָרֶ֥יךָ הַנְּעִימִֽים׃
Do not speak in the hearing of a fool,[^7] for he will despise the good sense of your words.
בְּאָזְנֵ֣י כְ֭סִיל אַל־תְּדַבֵּ֑ר כִּֽי־יָ֝ב֗וּז לְשֵׂ֣כֶל מִלֶּֽיךָ׃
Do not move an ancient boundary stone[^8] or encroach on the fields of the fatherless,
אַל־תַּ֭סֵּג גְּב֣וּל עוֹלָ֑ם וּבִשְׂדֵ֥י יְ֝תוֹמִ֗ים אַל־תָּבֹֽא׃
for their redeemer[^9] is strong; he will plead their case against you.
כִּֽי־גֹאֲלָ֥ם חָזָ֑ק הֽוּא־יָרִ֖יב אֶת־רִיבָ֣ם אִתָּֽךְ׃
Apply your heart to discipline[^10] and your ears to words of knowledge.
הָבִ֣יאָה לַמּוּסָ֣ר לִבֶּ֑ךָ וְ֝אָזְנֶ֗ךָ לְאִמְרֵי־דָֽעַת׃
Do not withhold discipline from a child; if you strike him with a rod, he will not die.
אַל־תִּמְנַ֣ע מִנַּ֣עַר מוּסָ֑ר כִּֽי־תַכֶּ֥נּוּ בַ֝שֵּׁ֗בֶט לֹ֣א יָמֽוּת׃
Strike him with the rod, and you will rescue his life from Sheol.[^11]
אַ֭תָּה בַּשֵּׁ֣בֶט תַּכֶּ֑נּוּ וְ֝נַפְשׁ֗וֹ מִשְּׁא֥וֹל תַּצִּֽיל׃
My son, if your heart is wise, my heart too will be glad,
בְּ֭נִי אִם־חָכַ֣ם לִבֶּ֑ךָ יִשְׂמַ֖ח לִבִּ֣י גַם־אָֽנִי׃
and my inmost being[^12] will rejoice when your lips speak what is right.
וְתַעְלֹ֥זְנָה כִלְיוֹתָ֑י בְּדַבֵּ֥ר שְׂ֝פָתֶ֗יךָ מֵישָׁרִֽים׃
Do not let your heart envy sinners, but continue[^13] in the fear of the LORD[^14] all day long.
אַל־יְקַנֵּ֣א לִ֭בְּךָ בַּֽחַטָּאִ֑ים כִּ֥י אִם־בְּיִרְאַת־יְ֝הוָ֗ה כָּל־הַיּֽוֹם׃
For surely there is a future, and your hope will not be cut off.
כִּ֭י אִם־יֵ֣שׁ אַחֲרִ֑ית וְ֝תִקְוָתְךָ֗ לֹ֣א תִכָּרֵֽת׃
Listen, my son, and be wise, and direct your heart in the way.
שְׁמַע־אַתָּ֣ה בְנִ֣י וַחֲכָ֑ם וְאַשֵּׁ֖ר בַּדֶּ֣רֶךְ לִבֶּֽךָ׃
Do not be among those who drink too much wine or those who gorge themselves on meat,
אַל־תְּהִ֥י בְסֹֽבְאֵי־יָ֑יִן בְּזֹלֲלֵ֖י בָשָׂ֣ר לָֽמוֹ׃
for the drunkard and the glutton will become poor, and drowsiness clothes them in rags.
כִּי־סֹבֵ֣א וְ֭זוֹלֵל יִוָּרֵ֑שׁ וּ֝קְרָעִ֗ים תַּלְבִּ֥ישׁ נוּמָֽה׃
Listen to your father, who gave you life, and do not despise your mother when she is old.
שְׁמַ֣ע לְ֭אָבִיךָ זֶ֣ה יְלָדֶ֑ךָ וְאַל־תָּ֝ב֗וּז כִּֽי־זָקְנָ֥ה אִמֶּֽךָ׃
Buy truth and do not sell it, wisdom, discipline and understanding.
אֱמֶ֣ת קְ֭נֵה וְאַל־תִּמְכֹּ֑ר חָכְמָ֖ה וּמוּסָ֣ר וּבִינָֽה׃
The father of a righteous person[^15] will greatly rejoice; whoever fathers a wise son will be glad in him.
*גול **גִּ֣יל *יגול **יָ֭גִיל אֲבִ֣י צַדִּ֑יק *יולד **וְיוֹלֵ֥ד חָ֝כָ֗ם *וישמח־**יִשְׂמַח־בּֽוֹ׃
Let your father and mother be glad; let her who bore you rejoice.
יִֽשְׂמַח־אָבִ֥יךָ וְאִמֶּ֑ךָ וְ֝תָגֵ֗ל יֽוֹלַדְתֶּֽךָ׃
My son, give me your heart, and let your eyes keep to my ways.[^16]
תְּנָֽה־בְנִ֣י לִבְּךָ֣ לִ֑י וְ֝עֵינֶ֗יךָ דְּרָכַ֥י *תרצנה **תִּצֽרְ[q]**ֹנָה׃
For a prostitute is a deep pit, and a foreign woman[^17] is a narrow well.
כִּֽי־שׁוּחָ֣ה עֲמֻקָּ֣ה זוֹנָ֑ה וּבְאֵ֥ר צָ֝רָ֗ה נָכְרִיָּֽה׃
She lies in wait like a robber and increases the number of the treacherous among men.
אַף־הִ֭יא כְּחֶ֣תֶף תֶּֽאֱרֹ֑ב וּ֝בוֹגְדִ֗ים בְּאָדָ֥ם תּוֹסִֽף׃
Who has woe? Who has sorrow? Who has quarrels? Who has complaints? Who has wounds for no reason? Who has bloodshot eyes?
לְמִ֨י א֥וֹי לְמִ֪י אֲב֡וֹי לְמִ֤י *מדונים **מִדְיָנִ֨ים ׀ לְמִ֥י שִׂ֗יחַ לְ֭מִי פְּצָעִ֣ים חִנָּ֑ם לְ֝מִ֗י חַכְלִל֥וּת עֵינָֽיִם׃
Those who linger over wine, who go to taste mixed wine.
לַֽמְאַחֲרִ֥ים עַל־הַיָּ֑יִן לַ֝בָּאִ֗ים לַחְקֹ֥ר מִמְסָֽךְ׃
Do not look at wine when it is red, when it sparkles in the cup,[^18] when it goes down smoothly.
אַל־תֵּ֥רֶא יַּיִן֮ כִּ֢י יִתְאַ֫דָּ֥ם כִּֽי־יִתֵּ֣ן *בכיס **בַּכּ֣וֹס עֵינ֑וֹ יִ֝תְהַלֵּ֗ךְ בְּמֵישָׁרִֽים׃
In the end it bites like a snake and stings like a viper.
אַ֭חֲרִיתוֹ כְּנָחָ֣שׁ יִשָּׁ֑ךְ וּֽכְצִפְעֹנִ֥י יַפְרִֽשׁ׃
Your eyes will see strange things,[^19] and your heart will speak perverse things.
עֵ֭ינֶיךָ יִרְא֣וּ זָר֑וֹת וְ֝לִבְּךָ֗ יְדַבֵּ֥ר תַּהְפֻּכֽוֹת׃
You will be like one who lies down in the middle of the sea, like one who lies on top of a mast.[^20]
וְ֭הָיִיתָ כְּשֹׁכֵ֣ב בְּלֶב־יָ֑ם וּ֝כְשֹׁכֵ֗ב בְּרֹ֣אשׁ חִבֵּֽל׃
"They hit me," you will say,[^21] "but I was not hurt; they beat me, but I did not feel it. When will I wake up? I will look for another drink."[^22]
הִכּ֥וּנִי בַל־חָלִיתִי֮ הֲלָמ֗וּנִי בַּל־יָ֫דָ֥עְתִּי מָתַ֥י אָקִ֑יץ א֝וֹסִ֗יף אֲבַקְשֶׁ֥נּוּ עֽוֹד׃

n.1: Or "who is before you".
n.2: Literally "if you are a master of appetite (*nephesh*)".
n.3: Literally "from your understanding (*binah*), stop". Or "have the sense to stop".
n.4: Literally "Will you let your eyes fly to it, and it is not?"
n.5: Literally "one who is evil of eye".
n.6: The Hebrew of this line is uncertain. Literally "for as he has calculated in his soul, so is he". With different vowels, the same consonants can be read "like a hair in his throat".
n.7: Hebrew *kesil* (see 1:22).
n.8: Compare 22:28.
n.9: Hebrew *go'el*, a relative whose duty was to defend a family member and buy back what he had lost (Leviticus 25:25; Ruth 4:4–6). Here probably God (compare 22:23).
n.10: Hebrew *musar*: discipline, training and correction (see 1:2). Also in verses 13 and 23.
n.11: Hebrew *Sheol*, the realm of the dead.
n.12: Literally "my kidneys", thought of as the seat of the emotions.
n.13: Literally "but in the fear of the LORD all day".
n.14: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.15: Hebrew *tsaddiq*: one who does what is right (see 2:20).
n.16: The Hebrew text is written "delight in my ways" but read "keep to my ways".
n.17: Hebrew *nokhriyyah*, "foreign woman" (see 2:16).
n.18: The Hebrew text is written "in the purse" but read "in the cup". Literally "when it gives its eye in the cup".
n.20: Hebrew *chibbel*, a word found only here, probably "mast" or "rigging".
n.21: The words *you will say* are not in the Hebrew. The verse gives the drunkard's own words.

v: Do not envy evil people, and do not desire to be with them,
אַל־תְּ֭קַנֵּא בְּאַנְשֵׁ֣י רָעָ֑ה וְאַל־*תתאו **תִּ֝תְאָ֗יו לִהְי֥וֹת אִתָּֽם׃
for their hearts plot violence, and their lips talk of trouble.
כִּי־שֹׁ֭ד יֶהְגֶּ֣ה לִבָּ֑ם וְ֝עָמָ֗ל שִׂפְתֵיהֶ֥ם תְּדַבֵּֽרְנָה׃
By wisdom a house is built, and by insight[^1] it is established;
בְּ֭חָכְמָה יִבָּ֣נֶה בָּ֑יִת וּ֝בִתְבוּנָ֗ה יִתְכּוֹנָֽן׃
by knowledge its rooms are filled with all kinds of precious and pleasant wealth.
וּ֭בְדַעַת חֲדָרִ֣ים יִמָּלְא֑וּ כָּל־ה֖וֹן יָקָ֣ר וְנָעִֽים׃
A wise man is strong,[^2] and a person of knowledge increases his strength,
גֶּֽבֶר־חָכָ֥ם בַּע֑וֹז וְאִֽישׁ־דַּ֝֗עַת מְאַמֶּץ־כֹּֽחַ׃
for by guidance[^3] you wage your war, and with many advisers there is victory.
כִּ֣י בְ֭תַחְבֻּלוֹת תַּעֲשֶׂה־לְּךָ֣ מִלְחָמָ֑ה וּ֝תְשׁוּעָ֗ה בְּרֹ֣ב יוֹעֵֽץ׃
Wisdom[^4] is too high for a fool;[^5] in the gate he does not open his mouth.
רָאמ֣וֹת לֶֽאֱוִ֣יל חָכְמ֑וֹת בַּ֝שַּׁ֗עַר לֹ֣א יִפְתַּח־פִּֽיהוּ׃
Whoever plans to do evil will be called a schemer.[^6]
מְחַשֵּׁ֥ב לְהָרֵ֑עַ ל֝֗וֹ בַּֽעַל־מְזִמּ֥וֹת יִקְרָֽאוּ׃
The scheming of folly[^7] is sin, and a mocker[^8] is detestable to people.
זִמַּ֣ת אִוֶּ֣לֶת חַטָּ֑את וְתוֹעֲבַ֖ת לְאָדָ֣ם לֵֽץ׃
If you lose heart in the day of trouble, your strength is small.[^9]
הִ֭תְרַפִּיתָ בְּי֥וֹם צָרָ֗ה צַ֣ר כֹּחֶֽכָה׃
Rescue those who are being taken away to death; hold back those who are staggering to the slaughter.
הַ֭צֵּל לְקֻחִ֣ים לַמָּ֑וֶת וּמָטִ֥ים לַ֝הֶ֗רֶג אִם־תַּחְשֽׂוֹךְ׃
If you say, "But we did not know this," does not the one who weighs hearts understand? Does not the one who guards your life know it? He will repay each person according to what he has done.[^10]
כִּֽי־תֹאמַ֗ר הֵן֮ לֹא־יָדַ֢עְנ֫וּ זֶ֥ה הֲ‍ֽלֹא־תֹ֘כֵ֤ן לִבּ֨וֹת ׀ הֽוּא־יָבִ֗ין וְנֹצֵ֣ר נַ֭פְשְׁךָ ה֣וּא יֵדָ֑ע וְהֵשִׁ֖יב לְאָדָ֣ם כְּפָעֳלֽוֹ׃
Eat honey, my son, for it is good, and the honeycomb is sweet to your taste.
אֱכָל־בְּנִ֣י דְבַ֣שׁ כִּי־ט֑וֹב וְנֹ֥פֶת מָ֝ת֗וֹק עַל־חִכֶּֽךָ׃
Know that wisdom is like that for your soul; if you find it, there will be a future, and your hope will not be cut off.
כֵּ֤ן ׀ דְּעֶ֥ה חָכְמָ֗ה לְנַ֫פְשֶׁ֥ךָ אִם־מָ֭צָאתָ וְיֵ֣שׁ אַחֲרִ֑ית וְ֝תִקְוָתְךָ֗ לֹ֣א תִכָּרֵֽת׃ פ
Do not lie in wait like a wicked man[^11] against the home of the righteous;[^12] do not destroy his resting place.
אַל־תֶּאֱרֹ֣ב רָ֭שָׁע לִנְוֵ֣ה צַדִּ֑יק אַֽל־תְּשַׁדֵּ֥ד רִבְצוֹ׃
For the righteous falls seven times and rises again, but the wicked stumble in times of disaster.
כִּ֤י שֶׁ֨בַע ׀ יִפּ֣וֹל צַדִּ֣יק וָקָ֑ם וּ֝רְשָׁעִ֗ים יִכָּשְׁל֥וּ בְרָעָֽה׃
Do not rejoice when your enemy[^13] falls, and do not let your heart be glad when he stumbles,
בִּנְפֹ֣ל *אויבי[y]*ך **אֽ֭וֹיִבְךָ אַל־תִּשְׂמָ֑ח וּ֝בִכָּשְׁל֗וֹ אַל־יָגֵ֥ל לִבֶּֽךָ׃
or the LORD[^14] will see it and be displeased, and turn his anger away from him.
פֶּן־יִרְאֶ֣ה יְ֭הוָה וְרַ֣ע בְּעֵינָ֑יו וְהֵשִׁ֖יב מֵעָלָ֣יו אַפּֽוֹ׃
Do not fret because of evildoers or envy the wicked,
אַל־תִּתְחַ֥ר בַּמְּרֵעִ֑ים אַל־תְּ֝קַנֵּ֗א בָּרְשָׁעִֽים׃
for the evil person has no future; the lamp of the wicked will be snuffed out.
כִּ֤י ׀ לֹֽא־תִהְיֶ֣ה אַחֲרִ֣ית לָרָ֑ע נֵ֖ר רְשָׁעִ֣ים יִדְעָֽךְ׃
My son, fear the LORD and the king; do not associate with those who are given to change,[^15]
יְרָֽא־אֶת־יְהוָ֣ה בְּנִ֣י וָמֶ֑לֶךְ עִם־שׁ֝וֹנִ֗ים אַל־תִּתְעָרָֽב׃
for disaster from them will rise suddenly, and who knows the ruin the two of them can bring?[^16]
כִּֽי־פִ֭תְאֹם יָק֣וּם אֵידָ֑ם וּפִ֥יד שְׁ֝נֵיהֶ֗ם מִ֣י יוֹדֵֽעַ׃ ס
These also are sayings of the wise.[^17] Showing partiality[^18] in judgment is not good.
גַּם־אֵ֥לֶּה לַֽחֲכָמִ֑ים הַֽכֵּר־פָּנִ֖ים בְּמִשְׁפָּ֣ט בַּל־טֽוֹב׃
Whoever says to the wicked, "You are righteous," peoples will curse him, nations will denounce him.
אֹ֤מֵ֨ר ׀ לְרָשָׁע֮ צַדִּ֢יק אָ֥תָּה יִקְּבֻ֥הוּ עַמִּ֑ים יִזְעָמ֥וּהוּ לְאֻמִּֽים׃
But those who rebuke the wicked will find delight, and a good blessing will come upon them.
וְלַמּוֹכִיחִ֥ים יִנְעָ֑ם וַֽ֝עֲלֵיהֶ֗ם תָּב֥וֹא בִרְכַּת־טֹֽוּב׃
Whoever gives an honest answer kisses the lips.[^19]
שְׂפָתַ֥יִם יִשָּׁ֑ק מֵ֝שִׁ֗יב דְּבָרִ֥ים נְכֹחִֽים׃
Put your outdoor work in order and get your fields ready; after that, build your house.[^20]
הָ֘כֵ֤ן בַּח֨וּץ ׀ מְלַאכְתֶּ֗ךָ וְעַתְּדָ֣הּ בַּשָּׂדֶ֣ה לָ֑ךְ אַ֝חַ֗ר וּבָנִ֥יתָ בֵיתֶֽךָ׃ פ
Do not be a witness against your neighbor without cause; would you deceive with your lips?
אַל־תְּהִ֣י עֵד־חִנָּ֣ם בְּרֵעֶ֑ךָ וַ֝הֲפִתִּ֗יתָ בִּשְׂפָתֶֽיךָ׃
Do not say, "I will do to him as he has done to me; I will pay the man back for what he has done."
אַל־תֹּאמַ֗ר כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר עָֽשָׂה־לִ֭י כֵּ֤ן אֶֽעֱשֶׂה־לּ֑וֹ אָשִׁ֖יב לָאִ֣ישׁ כְּפָעֳלֽוֹ׃
I passed by the field of a lazy man,[^21] by the vineyard of a man who lacked sense,[^22]
עַל־שְׂדֵ֣ה אִישׁ־עָצֵ֣ל עָבַ֑רְתִּי וְעַל־כֶּ֝֗רֶם אָדָ֥ם חֲסַר־לֵֽב׃
and look, it was all overgrown with thistles; its surface was covered with weeds, and its stone wall was broken down.
וְהִנֵּ֨ה עָ֘לָ֤ה כֻלּ֨וֹ ׀ קִמְּשֹׂנִ֗ים כָּסּ֣וּ פָנָ֣יו חֲרֻלִּ֑ים וְגֶ֖דֶר אֲבָנָ֣יו נֶהֱרָֽסָה׃
I looked and took it to heart; I saw and received discipline:[^23]
וָֽאֶחֱזֶ֣ה אָ֭נֹכִֽי אָשִׁ֣ית לִבִּ֑י רָ֝אִ֗יתִי לָקַ֥חְתִּי מוּסָּֽר׃
a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest,
מְעַ֣ט שֵׁ֭נוֹת מְעַ֣ט תְּנוּמ֑וֹת מְעַ֓ט ׀ חִבֻּ֖ק יָדַ֣יִם לִשְׁכָּֽב׃
and poverty will come on you like a prowler, and need like an armed man.[^24]
וּבָֽא־מִתְהַלֵּ֥ךְ רֵישֶׁ֑ךָ וּ֝מַחְסֹרֶ֗יךָ כְּאִ֣ישׁ מָגֵֽן׃ פ

n.1: Hebrew *tevunah* (see 2:2).
n.2: Literally "is in strength". The Septuagint reads "A wise man is better than a strong one".
n.3: Hebrew *tachbulot*, as in 1:5.
n.4: Hebrew *chokhmot*, as in 1:20.
n.5: Hebrew *ewil*, the morally perverse, stubborn fool (see 1:7).
n.6: Literally "a master of schemes". Hebrew *mezimmot*, as in 12:2.
n.7: Hebrew *iwwelet*, "folly", the word related to *ewil*, "fool" (see 1:7).
n.8: Hebrew *lets*: one who scorns wisdom and laughs at correction (see 1:22).
n.9: In Hebrew there is a play on *tsarah*, "trouble", and *tsar*, "small, narrow".
n.10: Compare Psalm 62:13 (62:12 in most English Bibles); Romans 2:6.
n.11: Or "Do not lie in wait, you wicked man". Hebrew *rasha* (see 2:22).
n.12: Hebrew *tsaddiq*: one who does what is right (see 2:20).
n.13: The Hebrew text is written "your enemies" but read "your enemy".
n.14: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.15: Hebrew *shonim*, "those who change", perhaps rebels. The Septuagint reads "and do not disobey either of them".
n.16: *The two of them* are probably the LORD and the king (verse 21).
n.17: A short collection follows (verses 23–34). From here to the end of the book the Septuagint arranges the material differently. After 24:22 it has 30:1–14, then 24:23–34, then 30:15–33 and 31:1–9, then chapters 25–29, and last 31:10–31.
n.18: Literally "Recognizing faces".
n.19: A kiss on the lips may have been a sign of friendship and loyalty.
n.22: Literally "lacking heart". In Hebrew thought the heart is the seat of understanding.

v: These also are proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied.[^1]
גַּם־אֵ֭לֶּה מִשְׁלֵ֣י שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶ֝עְתִּ֗יקוּ אַנְשֵׁ֤י ׀ חִזְקִיָּ֬ה מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָֽה׃
It is the glory of God to conceal a matter, and the glory of kings to search out a matter.
כְּבֹ֣ד אֱ֭לֹהִים הַסְתֵּ֣ר דָּבָ֑ר וּכְבֹ֥ד מְ֝לָכִ֗ים חֲקֹ֣ר דָּבָֽר׃
As the heavens are high and the earth is deep, so the heart of kings is unsearchable.
שָׁמַ֣יִם לָ֭רוּם וָאָ֣רֶץ לָעֹ֑מֶק וְלֵ֥ב מְ֝לָכִ֗ים אֵ֣ין חֵֽקֶר׃
Remove the dross from silver, and a vessel comes out for the silversmith.
הָג֣וֹ סִיגִ֣ים מִכָּ֑סֶף וַיֵּצֵ֖א לַצֹּרֵ֣ף כֶּֽלִי׃
Remove the wicked[^2] from the king's presence, and his throne will be established in righteousness.
הָג֣וֹ רָ֭שָׁע לִפְנֵי־מֶ֑לֶךְ וְיִכּ֖וֹן בַּצֶּ֣דֶק כִּסְאֽוֹ׃
Do not put yourself forward before the king, and do not stand in the place of the great,
אַל־תִּתְהַדַּ֥ר לִפְנֵי־מֶ֑לֶךְ וּבִמְק֥וֹם גְּ֝דֹלִ֗ים אַֽל־תַּעֲמֹֽד׃
for it is better to be told, "Come up here," than to be put lower in the presence of a noble whom your eyes have seen.[^3]
כִּ֤י ט֥וֹב אֲמָר־לְךָ֗ עֲ‍ֽלֵ֫ה הֵ֥נָּה מֵֽ֭הַשְׁפִּ֣ילְךָ לִפְנֵ֣י נָדִ֑יב אֲשֶׁ֖ר רָא֣וּ עֵינֶֽיךָ׃
Do not go out hastily to court, for what will you do in the end, when your neighbor puts you to shame?
אַל־תֵּצֵ֥א לָרִ֗ב מַ֫הֵ֥ר פֶּ֣ן מַה־תַּ֭עֲשֶׂה בְּאַחֲרִיתָ֑הּ בְּהַכְלִ֖ים אֹתְךָ֣ רֵעֶֽךָ׃
Argue your case with your neighbor, but do not reveal another's secret,
רִֽ֭יבְךָ רִ֣יב אֶת־רֵעֶ֑ךָ וְס֖וֹד אַחֵ֣ר אַל־תְּגָֽל׃
or the one who hears it will disgrace you,[^4] and your bad name will never go away.
פֶּֽן־יְחַסֶּדְךָ֥ שֹׁמֵ֑עַ וְ֝דִבָּתְךָ֗ לֹ֣א תָשֽׁוּב׃
Like apples of gold in settings of silver is a word spoken at the right time.[^5]
תַּפּוּחֵ֣י זָ֭הָב בְּמַשְׂכִּיּ֣וֹת כָּ֑סֶף דָּ֝בָ֗ר דָּבֻ֥ר עַל־אָפְנָֽיו׃
Like a gold earring or an ornament of fine gold is a wise person who corrects a listening ear.
נֶ֣זֶם זָ֭הָב וַחֲלִי־כָ֑תֶם מוֹכִ֥יחַ חָ֝כָ֗ם עַל־אֹ֥זֶן שֹׁמָֽעַת׃
Like the coolness of snow at harvest time is a faithful messenger to those who send him; he refreshes the life of his masters.
כְּצִנַּת־שֶׁ֨לֶג ׀ בְּי֬וֹם קָצִ֗יר צִ֣יר נֶ֭אֱמָן לְשֹׁלְחָ֑יו וְנֶ֖פֶשׁ אֲדֹנָ֣יו יָשִֽׁיב׃ פ
Like clouds and wind without rain is a man who boasts of a gift he does not give.
נְשִׂיאִ֣ים וְ֭רוּחַ וְגֶ֣שֶׁם אָ֑יִן אִ֥ישׁ מִ֝תְהַלֵּ֗ל בְּמַתַּת־שָֽׁקֶר׃
With patience a ruler can be persuaded, and a gentle tongue can break a bone.
בְּאֹ֣רֶךְ אַ֭פַּיִם יְפֻתֶּ֣ה קָצִ֑ין וְלָשׁ֥וֹן רַ֝כָּ֗ה תִּשְׁבָּר־גָּֽרֶם׃
If you find honey, eat only what you need, or you will have too much and vomit it up.
דְּבַ֣שׁ מָ֭צָאתָ אֱכֹ֣ל דַּיֶּ֑ךָּ פֶּן־תִּ֝שְׂבָּעֶ֗נּוּ וַהֲקֵֽאתֽוֹ׃
Seldom set foot in your neighbor's house, or he will have too much of you and hate you.
הֹקַ֣ר רַ֭גְלְךָ מִבֵּ֣ית רֵעֶ֑ךָ פֶּן־יִ֝שְׂבָּעֲךָ֗ וּשְׂנֵאֶֽךָ׃
Like a club, a sword or a sharp arrow is a man who gives false testimony against his neighbor.
מֵפִ֣יץ וְ֭חֶרֶב וְחֵ֣ץ שָׁנ֑וּן אִ֥ישׁ עֹנֶ֥ה בְ֝רֵעֵ֗הוּ עֵ֣ד שָֽׁקֶר׃
Like a broken tooth or a lame foot is trust in a treacherous person in a time of trouble.
שֵׁ֣ן רֹ֭עָה וְרֶ֣גֶל מוּעָ֑דֶת מִבְטָ֥ח בּ֝וֹגֵ֗ד בְּי֣וֹם צָרֽ͏ָה׃
Like one who takes off a garment on a cold day, like vinegar on soda,[^6] is one who sings songs to a heavy heart.
מַ֥עֲדֶה בֶּ֨גֶד ׀ בְּי֣וֹם קָ֭רָה חֹ֣מֶץ עַל־נָ֑תֶר וְשָׁ֥ר בַּ֝שִּׁרִ֗ים עַ֣ל לֶב־רָֽע׃ פ
If your enemy[^7] is hungry, give him bread to eat; if he is thirsty, give him water to drink,
אִם־רָעֵ֣ב שֹׂ֭נַאֲךָ הַאֲכִלֵ֣הוּ לָ֑חֶם וְאִם־צָ֝מֵ֗א הַשְׁקֵ֥הוּ מָֽיִם׃
for you will heap burning coals on his head, and the LORD[^8] will reward you.[^9]
כִּ֤י גֶֽחָלִ֗ים אַ֭תָּה חֹתֶ֣ה עַל־רֹאשׁ֑וֹ וֽ͏ַ֝יהוָ֗ה יְשַׁלֶּם־לָֽךְ׃
The north wind brings forth rain, and a secret tongue, angry faces.
ר֣וּחַ צָ֭פוֹן תְּח֣וֹלֵֽל גָּ֑שֶׁם וּפָנִ֥ים נִ֝זְעָמִ֗ים לְשׁ֣וֹן סָֽתֶר׃
Better to live in a corner of the roof than in a house shared with a quarrelsome wife.[^10]
ט֗וֹב שֶׁ֥בֶת עַל־פִּנַּת־גָּ֑ג מֵאֵ֥שֶׁת *מדונים **מִ֝דְיָנִ֗ים וּבֵ֥ית חָֽבֶר׃
Like cold water to a weary soul is good news from a distant land.
מַ֣יִם קָ֭רִים עַל־נֶ֣פֶשׁ עֲיֵפָ֑ה וּשְׁמוּעָ֥ה ט֝וֹבָ֗ה מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מֶרְחָֽק׃
Like a muddied spring or a polluted fountain is a righteous person[^11] who gives way before the wicked.
מַעְיָ֣ן נִ֭רְפָּשׂ וּמָק֣וֹר מָשְׁחָ֑ת צַ֝דִּ֗יק מָ֣ט לִפְנֵֽי־רָשָֽׁע׃
It is not good to eat much honey, nor is it glorious to seek one's own glory.[^12]
אָ֘כֹ֤ל דְּבַ֣שׁ הַרְבּ֣וֹת לֹּא־ט֑וֹב וְחֵ֖קֶר כְּבֹדָ֣ם כָּבֽוֹד׃
Like a city broken into and left without walls is a person who has no control over his spirit.
עִ֣יר פְּ֭רוּצָה אֵ֣ין חוֹמָ֑ה אִ֝֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֤ר אֵ֖ין מַעְצָ֣ר לְרוּחֽוֹ׃

n.1: A new collection begins here (chapters 25–29). Hezekiah reigned more than two centuries after Solomon (2 Kings 18–20).
n.2: Hebrew *rasha*: one who is guilty of wrong (see 2:22).
n.3: Or "What your eyes have seen, (8) do not bring hastily to court". Compare Luke 14:8–10.
n.4: Hebrew *yechassedkha*, from the verb related to *chesed*, "disgrace" (14:34).
n.5: Literally "on its wheels", probably "at the right time" or "in the right way".
n.6: Hebrew *neter*, natron or soda, which fizzes when vinegar is poured on it.
n.7: Literally "the one who hates you".
n.8: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.9: Romans 12:20 quotes verses 21–22.
n.10: The verse repeats 21:9.
n.11: Hebrew *tsaddiq*: one who does what is right (see 2:20).
n.12: The Hebrew of this line is difficult. Literally "and searching out their glory is glory". The translation carries over the "not" of the first line.

v: Like snow in summer and like rain at harvest, so honor is not fitting for a fool.[^1]
כַּשֶּׁ֤לֶג ׀ בַּקַּ֗יִץ וְכַמָּטָ֥ר בַּקָּצִ֑יר כֵּ֤ן לֹא־נָאוֶ֖ה לִכְסִ֣יל כָּבֽוֹד׃
Like a sparrow flitting, like a swallow flying, so an undeserved curse comes home to the one who utters it.[^2]
כַּצִּפּ֣וֹר לָ֭נוּד כַּדְּר֣וֹר לָע֑וּף כֵּ֥ן קִֽלְלַ֥ת חִ֝נָּ֗ם *לא **ל֣וֹ תָבֹֽא׃
A whip for the horse, a bridle for the donkey, and a rod for the backs of fools.
שׁ֣וֹט לַ֭סּוּס מֶ֣תֶג לַחֲמ֑וֹר וְ֝שֵׁ֗בֶט לְגֵ֣ו כְּסִילִֽים׃
Do not answer a fool according to his folly,[^3] or you will be like him yourself.
אַל־תַּ֣עַן כְּ֭סִיל כְּאִוַּלְתּ֑וֹ פֶּֽן־תִּשְׁוֶה־לּ֥וֹ גַם־אָֽתָּה׃
Answer a fool according to his folly, or he will be wise in his own eyes.[^4]
עֲנֵ֣ה כְ֭סִיל כְּאִוַּלְתּ֑וֹ פֶּן־יִהְיֶ֖ה חָכָ֣ם בְּעֵינָֽיו׃
Whoever sends a message by the hand of a fool cuts off his own feet and drinks violence.
מְקַצֶּ֣ה רַ֭גְלַיִם חָמָ֣ס שֹׁתֶ֑ה שֹׁלֵ֖חַ דְּבָרִ֣ים בְּיַד־כְּסִֽיל׃
Like the legs of a lame person, which hang useless, is a proverb in the mouth of fools.
דַּלְי֣וּ שֹׁ֭קַיִם מִפִּסֵּ֑חַ וּ֝מָשָׁ֗ל בְּפִ֣י כְסִילִֽים׃
Like tying a stone in a sling[^5] is giving honor to a fool.
כִּצְר֣וֹר אֶ֭בֶן בְּמַרְגֵּמָ֑ה כֵּן־נוֹתֵ֖ן לִכְסִ֣יל כָּבֽוֹד׃
Like a thorn that gets into the hand of a drunkard is a proverb in the mouth of fools.
