ח֭וֹחַ עָלָ֣ה בְיַד־שִׁכּ֑וֹר וּ֝מָשָׁ֗ל בְּפִ֣י כְסִילִֽים׃
Like an archer who wounds everyone is one who hires a fool or hires passersby.[^6]
רַ֥ב מְחֽוֹלֵֽל־כֹּ֑ל וְשֹׂכֵ֥ר כְּ֝סִ֗יל וְשֹׂכֵ֥ר עֹבְרִֽים׃
Like a dog that returns to its vomit is a fool who repeats his folly.[^7]
כְּ֭כֶלֶב שָׁ֣ב עַל־קֵא֑וֹ כְּ֝סִ֗יל שׁוֹנֶ֥ה בְאִוַּלְתּֽוֹ׃
Do you see a person wise in his own eyes? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
רָאִ֗יתָ אִ֭ישׁ חָכָ֣ם בְּעֵינָ֑יו תִּקְוָ֖ה לִכְסִ֣יל מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃
The lazy person[^8] says, "There is a lion in the road! A lion in the streets!"[^9]
אָמַ֣ר עָ֭צֵל שַׁ֣חַל בַּדָּ֑רֶךְ אֲ֝רִ֗י בֵּ֣ין הָרְחֹבֽוֹת׃
As a door turns on its hinges, so the lazy person turns on his bed.
הַ֭דֶּלֶת תִּסּ֣וֹב עַל־צִירָ֑הּ וְ֝עָצֵ֗ל עַל־מִטָּתֽוֹ׃
The lazy person buries his hand in the dish; he is too tired to bring it back to his mouth.[^10]
טָ֘מַ֤ן עָצֵ֣ל יָ֭דוֹ בַּצַּלָּ֑חַת נִ֝לְאָ֗ה לַֽהֲשִׁיבָ֥הּ אֶל־פִּֽיו׃
The lazy person is wiser in his own eyes than seven people who answer sensibly.
חָכָ֣ם עָצֵ֣ל בְּעֵינָ֑יו מִ֝שִּׁבְעָ֗ה מְשִׁ֣יבֵי טָֽעַם׃
Like one who grabs a dog by the ears is a passerby who meddles[^11] in a quarrel not his own.
מַחֲזִ֥יק בְּאָזְנֵי־כָ֑לֶב עֹבֵ֥ר מִ֝תְעַבֵּ֗ר עַל־רִ֥יב לֹּֽא־לֽוֹ׃
Like a madman who shoots flaming arrows, arrows and death,
כְּֽ֭מִתְלַהְלֵהַּ הַיֹּרֶ֥ה זִקִּ֗ים חִצִּ֥ים וָמָֽוֶת׃
so is the man who deceives his neighbor and says, "I was only joking!"
כֵּֽן־אִ֭ישׁ רִמָּ֣ה אֶת־רֵעֵ֑הוּ וְ֝אָמַ֗ר הֲ‍ֽלֹא־מְשַׂחֵ֥ק אָֽנִי׃
Without wood a fire goes out, and without a gossip[^12] a quarrel dies down.
בְּאֶ֣פֶס עֵ֭צִים תִּכְבֶּה־אֵ֑שׁ וּבְאֵ֥ין נִ֝רְגָּ֗ן יִשְׁתֹּ֥ק מָדֽוֹן׃
As charcoal to embers and wood to fire, so is a quarrelsome man for kindling strife.
פֶּחָ֣ם לְ֭גֶחָלִים וְעֵצִ֣ים לְאֵ֑שׁ וְאִ֥ישׁ *מדונים **מִ֝דְיָנִ֗ים לְחַרְחַר־רִֽיב׃ פ
The words of a gossip are like tasty morsels; they go down into the inner parts of the body.[^13]
דִּבְרֵ֣י נִ֭רְגָּן כְּמִֽתְלַהֲמִ֑ים וְ֝הֵ֗ם יָרְד֥וּ חַדְרֵי־בָֽטֶן׃
Like glaze[^14] coating an earthenware pot are burning lips with an evil heart.
כֶּ֣סֶף סִ֭יגִים מְצֻפֶּ֣ה עַל־חָ֑רֶשׂ שְׂפָתַ֖יִם דֹּלְקִ֣ים וְלֶב־רָֽע׃
Whoever hates disguises it with his lips, but inside he harbors deceit.
*בשפתו **בִּ֭שְׂפָתָיו יִנָּכֵ֣ר שׂוֹנֵ֑א וּ֝בְקִרְבּ֗וֹ יָשִׁ֥ית מִרְמָֽה׃
When he speaks graciously, do not believe him, for seven detestable things[^15] are in his heart.
כִּֽי־יְחַנֵּ֣ן ק֭וֹלוֹ אַל־תַּֽאֲמֶן־בּ֑וֹ כִּ֤י שֶׁ֖בַע תּוֹעֵב֣וֹת בְּלִבּֽוֹ׃
His hatred may be covered by deception, but his evil will be exposed in the assembly.
תִּכַּסֶּ֣ה שִׂ֭נְאָה בְּמַשָּׁא֑וֹן תִּגָּלֶ֖ה רָעָת֣וֹ בְקָהָֽל׃
Whoever digs a pit will fall into it, and a stone will come back on the one who rolls it.
כֹּֽרֶה־שַּׁ֭חַת בָּ֣הּ יִפֹּ֑ל וְגֹ֥לֵ֥ל אֶ֝בֶן אֵלָ֥יו תָּשֽׁוּב׃
A lying tongue hates those it crushes,[^16] and a flattering mouth works ruin.
לְֽשׁוֹן־שֶׁ֭קֶר יִשְׂנָ֣א דַכָּ֑יו וּפֶ֥ה חָ֝לָ֗ק יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה מִדְחֶֽה׃

n.1: Hebrew *kesil*, the most common word for "fool" in Proverbs: someone dull and self-satisfied who does not want to learn (see 1:22). Throughout verses 1–12.
n.2: Literally "comes to him", probably the one who utters it. The Hebrew text is written "does not come", which gives the sense "so an undeserved curse does not land".
n.3: Hebrew *iwwelet*, "folly", the word related to *ewil*, "fool" (see 1:7). Also in verses 5 and 11.
n.4: Verses 4 and 5 are set side by side, giving opposite advice.
n.5: Or "Like a bag of precious stones in a heap of stones".
n.6: The Hebrew of this verse is very uncertain. Literally "Much (or 'An archer', or 'A master') wounding (or 'producing') all, and one who hires a fool and one who hires passersby".
n.7: 2 Peter 2:22 quotes the first line.
n.8: Hebrew *atsel*, traditionally "sluggard" (see 6:6). Also in verses 14–16.
n.9: Two different Hebrew words for "lion". Compare 22:13.
n.10: Compare 19:24.
n.11: Hebrew *mit'abber*, usually "becomes enraged"; here probably "gets involved".
n.12: Hebrew *nirgan*, "whisperer", as in 16:28. Also in verse 22.
n.13: The verse repeats 18:8.
n.14: The Hebrew vowel points read "silver of dross". The same consonants, divided into words differently, can be read "like glaze", a word known from other ancient languages.
n.15: Hebrew *to'evot*, plural of *to'evah*, "something loathsome" (see 3:32).
n.16: Literally "hates its crushed ones". The meaning is uncertain.

v: Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what a day may bring.
אַֽל־תִּ֭תְהַלֵּל בְּי֣וֹם מָחָ֑ר כִּ֤י לֹא־תֵ֝דַ֗ע מַה־יֵּ֥לֶד יֽוֹם׃
Let a stranger praise you, and not your own mouth, an outsider,[^1] and not your own lips.
יְהַלֶּלְךָ֣ זָ֣ר וְלֹא־פִ֑יךָ נָ֝כְרִ֗י וְאַל־שְׂפָתֶֽיךָ׃
A stone is heavy and sand is weighty, but a fool's provocation is heavier than both.[^2]
כֹּֽבֶד־אֶ֭בֶן וְנֵ֣טֶל הַח֑וֹל וְכַ֥עַס אֱ֝וִ֗יל כָּבֵ֥ד מִשְּׁנֵיהֶֽם׃
Wrath is cruel and anger is a flood, but who can stand before jealousy?
אַכְזְרִיּ֣וּת חֵ֭מָה וְשֶׁ֣טֶף אָ֑ף וּמִ֥י יַ֝עֲמֹד לִפְנֵ֥י קִנְאָֽה׃
Better open correction than hidden love.
ט֭וֹבָה תּוֹכַ֣חַת מְגֻלָּ֑ה מֵֽאַהֲבָ֥ה מְסֻתָּֽרֶת׃
Wounds from a friend can be trusted, but the kisses of an enemy are lavish.[^3]
נֶ֭אֱמָנִים פִּצְעֵ֣י אוֹהֵ֑ב וְ֝נַעְתָּר֗וֹת נְשִׁיק֥וֹת שׂוֹנֵֽא׃
One who is full tramples on honey, but to one who is hungry everything bitter is sweet.
נֶ֣פֶשׁ שְׂ֭בֵעָה תָּב֣וּס נֹ֑פֶת וְנֶ֥פֶשׁ רְ֝עֵבָ֗ה כָּל־מַ֥ר מָתֽוֹק׃
Like a bird that strays from its nest is a man who strays from his home.
כְּ֭צִפּוֹר נוֹדֶ֣דֶת מִן־קִנָּ֑הּ כֵּֽן־אִ֝֗ישׁ נוֹדֵ֥ד מִמְּקוֹמֽוֹ׃
Oil and incense make the heart glad, and the sweetness of a friend comes from heartfelt advice.[^4]
שֶׁ֣מֶן וּ֭קְטֹרֶת יְשַׂמַּֽח־לֵ֑ב וּמֶ֥תֶק רֵ֝עֵ֗הוּ מֵֽעֲצַת־נָֽפֶשׁ׃
Do not abandon your friend or your father's friend, and do not go to your brother's house on the day of your disaster. Better a neighbor nearby than a brother far away.
רֵ֥עֲךָ֨ *ורעה **וְרֵ֪עַ אָבִ֡יךָ אַֽל־תַּעֲזֹ֗ב וּבֵ֥ית אָחִ֗יךָ אַל־תָּ֭בוֹא בְּי֣וֹם אֵידֶ֑ךָ ט֥וֹב שָׁכֵ֥ן קָ֝ר֗וֹב מֵאָ֥ח רָחֽוֹק׃
Be wise, my son, and make my heart glad, so that I can answer anyone who taunts me.
חֲכַ֣ם בְּ֭נִי וְשַׂמַּ֣ח לִבִּ֑י וְאָשִׁ֖יבָה חֹרְפִ֣י דָבָֽר׃
The prudent[^5] sees danger and hides himself; the simple[^6] go on and pay for it.[^7]
עָר֤וּם רָאָ֣ה רָעָ֣ה נִסְתָּ֑ר פְּ֝תָאיִ֗ם עָבְר֥וּ נֶעֱנָֽשׁוּ׃
Take the garment of one who puts up security for a stranger; hold it in pledge for a foreign woman.[^8]
קַח־בִּ֭גְדוֹ כִּי־עָ֣רַב זָ֑ר וּבְעַ֖ד נָכְרִיָּ֣ה חַבְלֵֽהוּ׃
Whoever blesses his neighbor with a loud voice early in the morning, it will be counted to him as a curse.
מְבָ֘רֵ֤ךְ רֵעֵ֨הוּ ׀ בְּק֣וֹל גָּ֭דוֹל בַּבֹּ֣קֶר הַשְׁכֵּ֑ים קְ֝לָלָ֗ה תֵּחָ֥שֶׁב לֽוֹ׃
A constant dripping on a rainy day and a quarrelsome wife are alike;
דֶּ֣לֶף ט֭[t]וֹרֵד בְּי֣וֹם סַגְרִ֑יר וְאֵ֥שֶׁת *מדונים **מִ֝דְיָנִ֗ים נִשְׁתָּוָֽה׃
whoever restrains her restrains the wind or grasps oil with his right hand.[^9]
צֹפְנֶ֥יהָ צָֽפַן־ר֑וּחַ וְשֶׁ֖מֶן יְמִינ֣וֹ יִקְרָֽא׃
As iron sharpens iron, so one person sharpens another.[^10]
בַּרְזֶ֣ל בְּבַרְזֶ֣ל יָ֑חַד וְ֝אִ֗ישׁ יַ֣חַד פְּנֵֽי־רֵעֵֽהוּ׃
Whoever tends a fig tree will eat its fruit, and whoever looks after his master will be honored.
נֹצֵ֣ר תְּ֭אֵנָה יֹאכַ֣ל פִּרְיָ֑הּ וְשֹׁמֵ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣יו יְכֻבָּֽד׃
As water reflects the face, so the heart reflects the person.[^11]
כַּ֭מַּיִם הַפָּנִ֣ים לַפָּנִ֑ים כֵּ֤ן לֵֽב־הָ֝אָדָ֗ם לָאָדָֽם׃
Sheol and Abaddon[^12] are never satisfied, and human eyes are never satisfied.
שְׁא֣וֹל *ואבדה **וַ֭אֲבַדּוֹ לֹ֣א תִשְׂבַּ֑עְנָה וְעֵינֵ֥י הָ֝אָדָ֗ם לֹ֣א תִשְׂבַּֽעְנָה׃
The crucible is for silver and the furnace for gold, and a person is tested by the praise he receives.[^13]
מַצְרֵ֣ף לַ֭כֶּסֶף וְכ֣וּר לַזָּהָ֑ב וְ֝אִ֗ישׁ לְפִ֣י מַהֲלָלֽוֹ׃
Even if you pound a fool[^14] in a mortar, with a pestle among the grain, his folly will not leave him.
אִ֥ם תִּכְתּֽוֹשׁ־אֶת־הָאֱוִ֨יל ׀ בַּֽמַּכְתֵּ֡שׁ בְּת֣וֹךְ הָ֭רִיפוֹת בַּֽעֱלִ֑י לֹא־תָס֥וּר מֵ֝עָלָ֗יו אִוַּלְתּֽוֹ׃ פ
Know well the condition of your flocks; give careful attention to your herds,
יָדֹ֣עַ תֵּ֭דַע פְּנֵ֣י צֹאנֶ֑ךָ שִׁ֥ית לִ֝בְּךָ֗ לַעֲדָרִֽים׃
for riches do not last forever, and does a crown last for all generations?
כִּ֤י לֹ֣א לְעוֹלָ֣ם חֹ֑סֶן וְאִם־נֵ֝֗זֶר לְד֣וֹר *דור **וָדֽוֹר׃
When the grass is gone and the new growth appears, and the plants of the hills are gathered in,
גָּלָ֣ה חָ֭צִיר וְנִרְאָה־דֶ֑שֶׁא וְ֝נֶאֶסְפ֗וּ עִשְּׂב֥וֹת הָרִֽים׃
the lambs will provide your clothing, and the goats the price of a field,
כְּבָשִׂ֥ים לִלְבוּשֶׁ֑ךָ וּמְחִ֥יר שָׂ֝דֶ֗ה עַתּוּדִֽים׃
and there will be enough goats' milk for your food, for the food of your household, and to keep your servant girls alive.
וְדֵ֤י ׀ חֲלֵ֬ב עִזִּ֗ים לְֽ֭לַחְמְךָ לְלֶ֣חֶם בֵּיתֶ֑ךָ וְ֝חַיִּ֗ים לְנַעֲרוֹתֶֽיךָ׃

n.1: Hebrew *zar* and *nokhri*, the masculine forms of the words used for the "strange woman" and the "foreign woman" (2:16).
n.2: Hebrew *ewil*, the morally perverse, stubborn fool (see 1:7).
n.3: Hebrew *na'tarot*, perhaps "many, lavish", or "deceitful".
n.4: The Hebrew of this line is uncertain. Literally "and the sweetness of his friend from the advice of the soul". Or "and the sweetness of a friend is better than one's own advice".
n.5: Hebrew *arum*, "shrewd, prudent" (see 1:4).
n.6: Hebrew *peta'im*, plural of *peti*: naive, inexperienced people, easily led (see 1:4).
n.7: The verse repeats 22:3.
n.8: Hebrew *nokhriyyah*, "foreign woman" (see 2:16). The verse repeats 20:16.
n.9: The Hebrew of this verse is obscure. Literally "Those who hide her hide wind, and oil his right hand meets".
n.10: Literally "so a man sharpens the face of his friend".
n.11: Literally "As in water face to face, so the heart of a person to a person". This may mean that a person's heart shows what he is, or that one sees oneself in another's heart.
n.12: Hebrew *Sheol*, the realm of the dead, and *Abaddon*, "Destruction", another name for it (see 15:11).
n.13: Literally "and a man according to his praise". It may mean that a person is tested by how he takes praise, or known by what he praises.
n.14: Hebrew *ewil*, as in verse 3. *Folly* is *iwwelet*, the related word.

v: The wicked[^1] flee when no one pursues, but the righteous[^2] are as bold as a lion.
נָ֣סוּ וְאֵין־רֹדֵ֣ף רָשָׁ֑ע וְ֝צַדִּיקִ֗ים כִּכְפִ֥יר יִבְטָֽח׃
When a land rebels, it has many rulers, but through a person who understands and knows, its stability lasts.[^3]
בְּפֶ֣שַֽׁע אֶ֭רֶץ רַבִּ֣ים שָׂרֶ֑יהָ וּבְאָדָ֥ם מֵבִ֥ין יֹ֝דֵ֗עַ כֵּ֣ן יַאֲרִֽיךְ׃
A poor man who oppresses the poor is like a driving rain that leaves no food.
גּ[t]בֶר[t] רָ֭שׁ וְעֹשֵׁ֣ק דַּלִּ֑ים מָטָ֥ר סֹ֝חֵ֗ף וְאֵ֣ין לָֽחֶם׃
Those who abandon the law[^4] praise the wicked, but those who keep the law fight against them.
עֹזְבֵ֣י ת֭וֹרָה יְהַֽלְל֣וּ רָשָׁ֑ע וְשֹׁמְרֵ֥י ת֝וֹרָ֗ה יִתְגָּ֥רוּ בָֽם׃ פ
Evil people do not understand justice, but those who seek the LORD[^5] understand everything.
אַנְשֵׁי־רָ֭ע לֹא־יָבִ֣ינוּ מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וּמְבַקְשֵׁ֥י יְ֝הוָ֗ה יָבִ֥ינוּ כֹֽל׃
Better a poor person who walks in integrity than one whose ways are crooked,[^6] even if he is rich.
טֽוֹב־רָ֭שׁ הוֹלֵ֣ךְ בְּתֻמּ֑וֹ מֵעִקֵּ֥שׁ דְּ֝רָכַ֗יִם וְה֣וּא עָשִֽׁיר׃
Whoever keeps the law is a discerning son, but a companion of gluttons shames his father.
נוֹצֵ֣ר תּ֭וֹרָה בֵּ֣ן מֵבִ֑ין וְרֹעֶ֥[t]ה זֽ֝וֹלְלִ֗ים יַכְלִ֥ים אָבִֽיו׃
Whoever increases his wealth by interest and profit[^7] gathers it for one who is kind to the poor.
מַרְבֶּ֣ה ה֭וֹנוֹ בְּנֶ֣שֶׁךְ *ובתרבית **וְתַרְבִּ֑ית לְחוֹנֵ֖ן דַּלִּ֣ים יִקְבְּצֶֽנּוּ׃
Whoever turns his ear away from hearing the law, even his prayer is detestable.
מֵסִ֣יר אָ֭זְנוֹ מִשְּׁמֹ֣עַ תּוֹרָ֑ה גַּ֥ם תְּ֝פִלָּת֗וֹ תּוֹעֵבָֽה׃
Whoever leads the upright astray into an evil way will fall into his own pit, but the blameless will inherit good.
מַשְׁגֶּ֤ה יְשָׁרִ֨ים ׀ בְּדֶ֥רֶךְ רָ֗ע בִּשְׁחוּת֥וֹ הֽוּא־יִפּ֑וֹל וּ֝תְמִימִ֗ים יִנְחֲלוּ־טֽוֹב׃
A rich man is wise in his own eyes, but a poor man who is discerning sees through him.
חָכָ֣ם בְּ֭עֵינָיו אִ֣ישׁ עָשִׁ֑יר וְדַ֖ל מֵבִ֣ין יַחְקְרֶֽנּוּ׃
When the righteous triumph, there is great glory, but when the wicked rise, people hide.[^8]
בַּעֲלֹ֣ץ צַ֭דִּיקִים רַבָּ֣ה תִפְאָ֑רֶת וּבְק֥וּם רְ֝שָׁעִ֗ים יְחֻפַּ֥שׂ אָדָֽם׃
Whoever covers his offenses will not prosper, but whoever confesses and abandons them will find mercy.
מְכַסֶּ֣ה פְ֭שָׁעָיו לֹ֣א יַצְלִ֑יחַ וּמוֹדֶ֖ה וְעֹזֵ֣ב יְרֻחָֽם׃
Happy[^9] is the one who is always reverent,[^10] but whoever hardens his heart will fall into trouble.
אַשְׁרֵ֣י אָ֭דָם מְפַחֵ֣ד תָּמִ֑יד וּמַקְשֶׁ֥ה לִ֝בּ֗וֹ יִפּ֥וֹל בְּרָעָֽה׃
Like a roaring lion or a charging bear is a wicked ruler over a poor people.
אֲרִי־נֹ֭הֵם וְדֹ֣ב שׁוֹקֵ֑ק מֹשֵׁ֥ל רָ֝שָׁ֗ע עַ֣ל עַם־דָּֽל׃
A ruler who lacks insight[^11] is a great oppressor, but whoever hates unjust gain will live long.
נָגִ֗יד חֲסַ֣ר תְּ֭בוּנוֹת וְרַ֥ב מַעֲשַׁקּ֑וֹת *שנאי **שֹׂ֥נֵא בֶ֝֗צַע יַאֲרִ֥יךְ יָמִֽים׃ פ
A man burdened with someone's blood will be a fugitive until the Pit;[^12] let no one hold him back.
אָ֭דָם עָשֻׁ֣ק בְּדַם־נָפֶשׁ[c] עַד־בּ֥וֹר יָ֝נ֗וּס אַל־יִתְמְכוּ־בֽוֹ׃
Whoever walks blamelessly will be kept safe, but whoever is crooked in his ways will fall all at once.
הוֹלֵ֣ךְ תָּ֭מִים יִוָּשֵׁ֑עַ וְנֶעְקַ֥שׁ דְּ֝רָכַ֗יִם יִפּ֥וֹל בְּאֶחָֽת׃
Whoever works his land will have plenty of bread, but whoever chases worthless things will have plenty of poverty.
עֹבֵ֣ד אַ֭דְמָתוֹ יִֽשְׂבַּֽע־לָ֑חֶם וּמְרַדֵּ֥ף רֵ֝קִ֗ים יִֽשְׂבַּֽע־רִֽישׁ׃
A faithful person will have many blessings, but whoever hurries to get rich will not go unpunished.
אִ֣ישׁ אֱ֭מוּנוֹת רַב־בְּרָכ֑וֹת וְאָ֥ץ לְ֝הַעֲשִׁ֗יר לֹ֣א יִנָּקֶֽה׃
Showing partiality is not good, yet for a piece of bread a man will do wrong.
הַֽכֵּר־פָּנִ֥ים לֹא־ט֑וֹב וְעַל־פַּת־לֶ֝֗חֶם יִפְשַׁע־גָּֽבֶר׃
A stingy man[^13] hurries after wealth and does not know that poverty will come upon him.
נִֽבֳהָֽ[m]ל לַה֗וֹן אִ֭ישׁ רַ֣ע עָ֑יִן וְלֹֽא־יֵ֝דַע כִּי־חֶ֥סֶר יְבֹאֶֽנּוּ׃
Whoever corrects someone will in the end[^14] find more favor than one who flatters with his tongue.
מ֘וֹכִ֤יחַ אָדָ֣ם אַ֭חֲרַי חֵ֣ן יִמְצָ֑א מִֽמַּחֲלִ֥יק לָשֽׁוֹן׃
Whoever robs his father or his mother and says, "It is no offense," is a companion of a destroyer.
גּוֹזֵ֤ל ׀ אָ֘בִ֤יו וְאִמּ֗וֹ וְאֹמֵ֥ר אֵֽין־פָּ֑שַׁע חָבֵ֥ר ה֝֗וּא לְאִ֣ישׁ מַשְׁחִֽית׃
The greedy person[^15] stirs up strife, but whoever trusts in the LORD will prosper.
רְחַב־נֶ֭פֶשׁ יְגָרֶ֣ה מָד֑וֹן וּבוֹטֵ֖חַ עַל־יְהוָ֣ה יְדֻשָּֽׁן׃
Whoever trusts in his own heart is a fool,[^16] but whoever walks in wisdom will be kept safe.
בּוֹטֵ֣חַ בְּ֭לִבּוֹ ה֣וּא כְסִ֑יל וְהוֹלֵ֥ךְ בְּ֝חָכְמָ֗ה ה֣וּא יִמָּלֵֽט׃
Whoever gives to the poor will not lack, but whoever shuts his eyes will receive many curses.
נוֹתֵ֣ן לָ֭רָשׁ אֵ֣ין מַחְס֑וֹר וּמַעְלִ֥ים עֵ֝ינָ֗יו רַב־מְאֵרֽוֹת׃
When the wicked rise, people hide, but when they perish, the righteous increase.
בְּק֣וּם רְ֭שָׁעִים יִסָּתֵ֣ר אָדָ֑ם וּ֝בְאָבְדָ֗ם יִרְבּ֥וּ צַדִּיקִֽים׃

n.1: Hebrew *rasha*: one who is guilty of wrong (see 2:22).
n.2: Hebrew *tsaddiqim*, plural of *tsaddiq*: those who do what is right (see 2:20).
n.3: The Hebrew of this line is difficult. Literally "but by a person who understands, who knows, so it lasts long".
n.4: Hebrew *torah*, "instruction", here probably God's law. Also in verses 7 and 9.
n.5: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.6: Literally "crooked of two ways", perhaps double-dealing. Also in verse 18. Compare 19:1.
n.7: Lending at interest to a fellow Israelite was forbidden (Leviticus 25:36–37).
n.8: Literally "a person must be searched for".
n.9: Hebrew *ashrei*: happy, fortunate; traditionally "blessed".
n.10: Literally "who fears always", that is, fears God, or fears doing wrong.
n.11: Literally "lacking insights". Hebrew *tevunot*, plural of *tevunah* (see 2:2).
n.12: That is, until death. Hebrew *bor*, "pit", as in 1:12.
n.13: Literally "A man with an evil eye".
n.14: Hebrew *acharai*, literally "after me", probably "afterward".
n.15: Literally "One who is wide of appetite (*nephesh*)".

v: Whoever is often corrected yet stays stiff-necked will suddenly be broken, and there will be no healing.
אִ֣ישׁ תּ֭וֹכָחוֹת מַקְשֶׁה־עֹ֑רֶף פֶּ֥תַע יִ֝שָּׁבֵ֗ר וְאֵ֣ין מַרְפֵּֽא׃
When the righteous[^1] increase, the people rejoice, but when the wicked[^2] rule, the people groan.
בִּרְב֣וֹת צַ֭דִּיקִים יִשְׂמַ֣ח הָעָ֑ם וּבִמְשֹׁ֥ל רָ֝שָׁ֗ע יֵאָ֥נַֽח עָֽם׃
A man who loves wisdom makes his father glad, but a companion of prostitutes squanders his wealth.
אִֽישׁ־אֹהֵ֣ב חָ֭כְמָה יְשַׂמַּ֣ח אָבִ֑יו וְרֹעֶ֥ה ז֝וֹנ֗וֹת יְאַבֶּד־הֽוֹן׃
By justice a king gives a land stability, but a man who exacts contributions[^3] tears it down.
מֶ֗לֶךְ בְּ֭מִשְׁפָּט יַעֲמִ֣יד אָ֑רֶץ וְאִ֖ישׁ תְּרוּמ֣וֹת יֶֽהֶרְסֶֽנָּה׃
A man who flatters his neighbor is spreading a net for his feet.[^4]
גֶּ֭בֶר מַחֲלִ֣יק עַל־רֵעֵ֑הוּ רֶ֝֗שֶׁת פּוֹרֵ֥שׂ עַל־פְּעָמָֽיו׃
An evil man is snared by his own offense, but the righteous sings and rejoices.
בְּפֶ֤שַֽׁע אִ֣ישׁ רָ֣ע מוֹקֵ֑שׁ וְ֝צַדִּ֗יק יָר֥וּן וְשָׂמֵֽחַ׃
The righteous knows the rights of the poor; the wicked has no such understanding.[^5]
יֹדֵ֣עַ צַ֭דִּיק דִּ֣ין דַּלִּ֑ים רָ֝שָׁ֗ע לֹא־יָבִ֥ין דָּֽעַת׃
Mockers[^6] set a city aflame, but the wise turn away anger.
אַנְשֵׁ֣י לָ֭צוֹן יָפִ֣יחוּ קִרְיָ֑ה וַ֝חֲכָמִ֗ים יָשִׁ֥יבוּ אָֽף׃
If a wise man goes to court with a fool,[^7] the fool rages and laughs,[^8] and there is no peace.
אִֽישׁ־חָכָ֗ם נִ֭שְׁפָּט אֶת־אִ֣ישׁ אֱוִ֑יל וְרָגַ֥ז וְ֝שָׂחַ֗ק וְאֵ֣ין נָֽחַת׃
Bloodthirsty men hate the blameless, and as for the upright, they seek his life.[^9]
אַנְשֵׁ֣י דָ֭מִים יִשְׂנְאוּ־תָ֑ם וִֽ֝ישָׁרִ֗ים יְבַקְשׁ֥וּ נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃
A fool[^10] gives full vent to his anger,[^11] but a wise person quietly holds it back.
כָּל־ר֭וּחוֹ יוֹצִ֣יא כְסִ֑יל וְ֝חָכָ֗ם בְּאָח֥וֹר יְשַׁבְּחֶֽנָּה׃
If a ruler listens to lies, all his officials become wicked.
מֹ֭שֵׁל מַקְשִׁ֣יב עַל־דְּבַר־שָׁ֑קֶר כָּֽל־מְשָׁרְתָ֥יו רְשָׁעִֽים׃
The poor and the oppressor meet together; the LORD[^12] gives light to the eyes of both.[^13]
רָ֤שׁ וְאִ֣ישׁ תְּכָכִ֣ים נִפְגָּ֑שׁוּ מֵ֤אִיר־עֵינֵ֖י שְׁנֵיהֶ֣ם יְהוֽ͏ָה׃
If a king judges the poor with faithfulness, his throne will be established forever.
מֶ֤לֶךְ שׁוֹפֵ֣ט בֶּֽאֱמֶ֣ת דַּלִּ֑ים כִּ֝סְא֗וֹ לָעַ֥ד יִכּֽוֹן׃
The rod and correction give wisdom, but a child left to himself brings shame to his mother.
שֵׁ֣בֶט וְ֭תוֹכַחַת יִתֵּ֣ן חָכְמָ֑ה וְנַ֥עַר מְ֝שֻׁלָּ֗ח מֵבִ֥ישׁ אִמּֽוֹ׃
When the wicked increase, offense increases, but the righteous will see their downfall.
בִּרְב֣וֹת רְ֭שָׁעִים יִרְבֶּה־פָּ֑שַׁע וְ֝צַדִּיקִ֗ים בְּֽמַפַּלְתָּ֥ם יִרְאֽוּ׃
Discipline your son, and he will give you rest; he will bring delight to your soul.
יַסֵּ֣ר בִּ֭נְךָ וִֽינִיחֶ֑ךָ וְיִתֵּ֖ן מַעֲדַנִּ֣ים לְנַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃ פ
Where there is no vision,[^14] the people run wild, but whoever keeps the law[^15] is happy.[^16]
בְּאֵ֣ין חָ֭זוֹן יִפָּ֣רַֽע עָ֑ם וְשֹׁמֵ֖ר תּוֹרָ֣ה אַשְׁרֵֽהוּ׃
A servant cannot be disciplined by words alone; though he understands, he will not respond.
בִּ֭דְבָרִים לֹא־יִוָּ֣סֶר עָ֑בֶד כִּֽי־יָ֝בִ֗ין וְאֵ֣ין מַעֲנֶֽה׃
Do you see someone who is hasty in his words? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
חָזִ֗יתָ אִ֭ישׁ אָ֣ץ בִּדְבָרָ֑יו תִּקְוָ֖ה לִכְסִ֣יל מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃
If someone pampers his servant from youth, in the end it will bring grief.[^17]
מְפַנֵּ֣ק מִנֹּ֣עַר עַבְדּ֑וֹ וְ֝אַחֲרִית֗וֹ יִהְיֶ֥ה מָנֽוֹן׃
An angry man stirs up strife, and a hot-tempered man commits many offenses.
אִֽישׁ־אַ֭ף יְגָרֶ֣ה מָד֑וֹן וּבַ֖עַל חֵמָ֣ה רַב־פָּֽשַׁע׃
A person's pride will bring him low, but the lowly in spirit will gain honor.
גַּאֲוַ֣ת אָ֭דָם תַּשְׁפִּילֶ֑נּוּ וּשְׁפַל־ר֝֗וּחַ יִתְמֹ֥ךְ כָּבֽוֹד׃
Whoever is a partner with a thief hates his own life; he hears the curse but does not testify.[^18]
חוֹלֵ֣ק עִם־גַּ֭נָּב שׂוֹנֵ֣א נַּפְשׁ֑וֹ אָלָ֥ה יִ֝שְׁמַ֗ע וְלֹ֣א יַגִּֽיד׃
Fear of people sets a snare, but whoever trusts in the LORD is kept safe.
חֶרְדַּ֣ת אָ֭דָם יִתֵּ֣ן מוֹקֵ֑שׁ וּבוֹטֵ֖חַ בַּיהוָ֣ה יְשֻׂגָּֽב׃
Many seek the favor of a ruler, but justice for a person comes from the LORD.
רַ֭בִּים מְבַקְשִׁ֣ים פְּנֵי־מוֹשֵׁ֑ל וּ֝מֵיְהוָ֗ה מִשְׁפַּט־אִֽישׁ׃
An unjust man is detestable to the righteous, and one whose way is upright is detestable to the wicked.
תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת צַ֭דִּיקִים אִ֣ישׁ עָ֑וֶל וְתוֹעֲבַ֖ת רָשָׁ֣ע יְשַׁר־דָּֽרֶךְ׃ פ

n.1: Hebrew *tsaddiqim*, plural of *tsaddiq*: those who do what is right (see 2:20).
n.2: Hebrew *rasha*: one who is guilty of wrong (see 2:22).
n.3: Hebrew *terumot*, "contributions", perhaps heavy taxes or bribes.
n.4: Either his neighbor's feet or his own.
n.5: Literally "the wicked does not understand knowledge".
n.6: Literally "Men of mockery". Hebrew *latson*, from the same root as *lets*, "mocker" (see 1:22).
n.7: Hebrew *ewil*, the morally perverse, stubborn fool (see 1:7).
n.8: Or "whether the wise man is angry or laughs".
n.9: Literally "and the upright seek his life". This may mean that the upright care for the blameless person's life, or that the bloodthirsty seek the life of the upright.
n.10: Hebrew *kesil* (see 1:22). Also in verse 20.
n.11: Literally "brings out all his spirit (*ruach*)".
n.12: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.13: Compare 22:2.
n.14: Hebrew *chazon*, a prophet's vision, revelation from God.
n.15: Hebrew *torah*, "instruction", here probably God's law.
n.17: Literally "and his end will be *manon*", a word found only here, of uncertain meaning: perhaps "grief", "insolence" or "an heir".
n.18: The *curse* is the public oath that called on witnesses to come forward (Leviticus 5:1).

v: The words of Agur son of Jakeh, the oracle.[^1] The man declares to Ithiel, to Ithiel and Ucal:[^2]
דִּבְרֵ֤י ׀ אָג֥וּר בִּן־יָקֶ֗ה הַמַּ֫שָּׂ֥א נְאֻ֣ם הַ֭גֶּבֶר לְאִֽיתִיאֵ֑ל לְאִ֖יתִיאֵ֣ל וְאֻכָֽל׃
Surely I am too stupid[^3] to be a man; I do not have human understanding.[^4]
כִּ֤י בַ֣עַר אָנֹכִ֣י מֵאִ֑ישׁ וְלֹֽא־בִינַ֖ת אָדָ֣ם לִֽי׃
I have not learned wisdom, nor do I have knowledge of the Holy One.[^5]
וְלֹֽא־לָמַ֥דְתִּי חָכְמָ֑ה וְדַ֖עַת קְדֹשִׁ֣ים אֵדָֽע׃

Who has gone up to heaven and come down? Who has gathered the wind in his fists? Who has wrapped up the waters in a cloak? Who has established all the ends of the earth? What is his name, and what is his son's name? Surely you know![^6]
מִ֤י עָלָֽה־שָׁמַ֨יִם ׀ וַיֵּרַ֡ד מִ֤י אָֽסַף־ר֨וּחַ ׀ בְּחָפְנָ֡יו מִ֤י צָֽרַר־מַ֨יִם ׀ בַּשִּׂמְלָ֗ה מִ֭י הֵקִ֣ים כָּל־אַפְסֵי־אָ֑רֶץ מַה־שְּׁמ֥וֹ וּמַֽה־שֶּׁם־בְּ֝נ֗וֹ כִּ֣י תֵדָֽע׃
Every word of God[^7] is refined; he is a shield to those who take refuge in him.
כָּל־אִמְּרַ֣ת אֱל֣וֹהַּ צְרוּפָ֑ה מָגֵ֥ן ה֝֗וּא לַֽחֹסִ֥ים בּֽוֹ׃
Do not add to his words, or he will rebuke you, and you will be found a liar.[^8]
אַל־תּ֥וֹסְףְּ עַל־דְּבָרָ֑יו פֶּן־יוֹכִ֖יחַ בְּךָ֣ וְנִכְזָֽבְתָּ׃ פ
Two things I ask of you; do not refuse me before I die:
שְׁ֭תַּיִם שָׁאַ֣לְתִּי מֵאִתָּ֑ךְ אַל־תִּמְנַ֥ע מִ֝מֶּ֗נִּי בְּטֶ֣רֶם אָמֽוּת׃
keep falsehood and lies far from me; give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with the bread I need,[^9]
שָׁ֤וְא ׀ וּֽדְבַר־כָּזָ֡ב הַרְחֵ֬ק מִמֶּ֗נִּי רֵ֣אשׁ וָ֭עֹשֶׁר אַל־תִּֽתֶּן־לִ֑י הַ֝טְרִיפֵ֗נִי לֶ֣חֶם חֻקִּֽי׃
or I may become full and deny you and say, "Who is the LORD?"[^10] or I may become poor and steal, and profane the name of my God.
פֶּ֥ן אֶשְׂבַּ֨ע ׀ וְכִחַשְׁתִּי֮ וְאָמַ֗רְתִּי מִ֥י יְה֫וָ֥ה וּפֶֽן־אִוָּרֵ֥שׁ וְגָנַ֑בְתִּי וְ֝תָפַ֗שְׂתִּי שֵׁ֣ם אֱלֹהָֽי׃ פ
Do not slander a servant to his master, or he will curse you, and you will be held guilty.
אַל־תַּלְשֵׁ֣ן עֶ֭בֶד אֶל־*אדנו **אֲדֹנָ֑יו פֶּֽן־יְקַלֶּלְךָ֥ וְאָשָֽׁמְתָּ׃
There are those[^11] who curse their father and do not bless their mother.
דּ֭וֹר אָבִ֣יו יְקַלֵּ֑ל וְאֶת־אִ֝מּ֗וֹ לֹ֣א יְבָרֵֽךְ׃
There are those who are pure in their own eyes, yet are not washed of their filth.
דּ֭וֹר טָה֣וֹר בְּעֵינָ֑יו וּ֝מִצֹּאָת֗וֹ לֹ֣א רֻחָֽץ׃
There are those whose eyes are so haughty, whose eyelids are lifted high.
דּ֭וֹר מָה־רָמ֣וּ עֵינָ֑יו וְ֝עַפְעַפָּ֗יו יִנָּשֵֽׂאוּ׃
There are those whose teeth are swords, whose jaws are knives, to devour the poor from the earth and the needy from among humankind.
דּ֤וֹר ׀ חֲרָב֣וֹת שִׁנָּיו֮ וּֽמַאֲכָל֢וֹת מְֽתַלְּעֹ֫תָ֥יו לֶאֱכֹ֣ל עֲנִיִּ֣ים מֵאֶ֑רֶץ וְ֝אֶבְיוֹנִ֗ים מֵאָדָֽם׃ פ
The leech[^12] has two daughters: "Give! Give!" There are three things that are never satisfied, four that never say, "Enough!":[^13]
לַ֥עֲלוּקָ֨ה ׀ שְׁתֵּ֥י בָנוֹת֮ הַ֤ב ׀ הַ֥ב שָׁל֣וֹשׁ הֵ֭נָּה לֹ֣א תִשְׂבַּ֑עְנָה אַ֝רְבַּ֗ע לֹא־אָ֥מְרוּ הֽוֹן׃
Sheol,[^14] the barren womb, land that is never satisfied with water, and fire that never says, "Enough!"
שְׁאוֹל֮ וְעֹ֢צֶ֫ר רָ֥חַם אֶ֭רֶץ לֹא־שָׂ֣בְעָה מַּ֑יִם וְ֝אֵ֗שׁ לֹא־אָ֥מְרָה הֽוֹן׃
The eye that mocks a father and scorns obedience[^15] to a mother will be pecked out by the ravens of the valley and eaten by the young vultures.[^16]
עַ֤יִן ׀ תִּֽלְעַ֣ג לְאָב֮ וְתָב֢וּז לִֽיקֲּהַ֫ת־אֵ֥ם יִקְּר֥וּהָ עֹרְבֵי־נַ֑חַל וְֽיֹאכְל֥וּהָ בְנֵי־נָֽשֶׁר׃ פ
There are three things too wonderful for me, four that I do not understand:
שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה הֵ֭מָּה נִפְלְא֣וּ מִמֶּ֑נִּי *וארבע **וְ֝אַרְבָּעָ֗ה לֹ֣א יְדַעְתִּֽים׃
the way of an eagle in the sky, the way of a snake on a rock, the way of a ship on the high seas, and the way of a man with a young woman.[^17]
דֶּ֤רֶךְ הַנֶּ֨שֶׁר ׀ בַּשָּׁמַיִם֮ דֶּ֥רֶךְ נָחָ֗שׁ עֲלֵ֫י צ֥וּר דֶּֽרֶךְ־אֳנִיָּ֥ה בְלֶב־יָ֑ם וְדֶ֖רֶךְ גֶּ֣בֶר בְּעַלְמָֽה׃
This is the way of an adulterous woman: she eats and wipes her mouth and says, "I have done nothing wrong."
כֵּ֤ן ׀ דֶּ֥רֶךְ אִשָּׁ֗ה מְנָ֫אָ֥פֶת אָ֭כְלָה וּמָ֣חֲתָה פִ֑יהָ וְ֝אָמְרָ֗ה לֹֽא־פָעַ֥לְתִּי אָֽוֶן׃ פ
Under three things the earth trembles, under four it cannot bear up:
תַּ֣חַת שָׁ֭לוֹשׁ רָ֣גְזָה אֶ֑רֶץ וְתַ֥חַת אַ֝רְבַּ֗ע לֹא־תוּכַ֥ל שְׂאֵֽת׃
a servant when he becomes king, a godless fool[^18] when he is filled with food,
תַּֽחַת־עֶ֭בֶד כִּ֣י יִמְל֑וֹךְ וְ֝נָבָ֗ל כִּ֣י יִֽשְׂבַּֽע־לָֽחֶם׃
an unloved woman when she gets a husband, and a servant girl when she takes the place of her mistress.
תַּ֣חַת שְׂ֭נוּאָה כִּ֣י תִבָּעֵ֑ל וְ֝שִׁפְחָ֗ה כִּֽי־תִירַ֥שׁ גְּבִרְתָּֽהּ׃ פ
Four things on earth are small, but they are exceedingly wise:
אַרְבָּ֣עָה הֵ֭ם קְטַנֵּי־אָ֑רֶץ וְ֝הֵ֗מָּה חֲכָמִ֥ים מְחֻכָּמִֽים׃
the ants are a people without strength, yet they store up their food in summer;
הַ֭נְּמָלִים עַ֣ם לֹא־עָ֑ז וַיָּכִ֖ינוּ בַקַּ֣יִץ לַחְמָֽם׃
the rock badgers[^19] are a people without power, yet they make their homes in the rocks;
שְׁ֭פַנִּים עַ֣ם לֹא־עָצ֑וּם וַיָּשִׂ֖ימוּ בַסֶּ֣לַע בֵּיתָֽם׃
the locusts have no king, yet they all go out in ranks;
מֶ֭לֶךְ אֵ֣ין לָאַרְבֶּ֑ה וַיֵּצֵ֖א חֹצֵ֣ץ כֻּלּֽוֹ׃
the lizard[^20] can be caught in the hand,[^21] yet it lives in kings' palaces.
שְׂ֭מָמִית בְּיָדַ֣יִם תְּתַפֵּ֑שׂ וְ֝הִ֗יא בְּהֵ֣יכְלֵי מֶֽלֶךְ׃ פ
There are three things that are stately in their stride, four that are stately in their walk:
שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה הֵ֭מָּה מֵיטִ֣יבֵי צָ֑עַד וְ֝אַרְבָּעָ֗ה מֵיטִ֥בֵי לָֽכֶת׃
the lion, mightiest among beasts, which does not turn back before anything;
לַ֭יִשׁ גִּבּ֣וֹר בַּבְּהֵמָ֑ה וְלֹא־יָ֝שׁ֗וּב מִפְּנֵי־כֹֽל׃
the strutting rooster,[^22] or the male goat, and a king with his army around him.[^23]
זַרְזִ֣יר מָתְנַ֣יִם אוֹ־תָ֑יִשׁ וּ֝מֶ֗לֶךְ אַלְק֥וּם עִמּֽוֹ׃
If you have been foolish, exalting yourself, or if you have been scheming, put your hand over your mouth.
אִם־נָבַ֥לְתָּ בְהִתְנַשֵּׂ֑א וְאִם־זַ֝מּ֗וֹתָ יָ֣ד לְפֶֽה׃
For pressing milk produces curds, pressing the nose produces blood, and pressing anger produces strife.[^24]
כִּ֤י מִ֪יץ חָלָ֡ב י֘וֹצִ֤יא חֶמְאָ֗ה וּֽמִיץ־אַ֭ף י֣וֹצִיא דָ֑ם וּמִ֥יץ אַ֝פַּ֗יִם י֣וֹצִיא רִֽיב׃ פ

n.1: Or "of Massa", an Arabian tribe descended from Ishmael (Genesis 25:14); also in 31:1. Nothing more is known of Agur, and it is not clear where his words end. On the order of chapters 30–31 in the Septuagint, see the note on 24:23.
n.2: With different vowels and a different division of the words, "I am weary, O God; I am weary, O God, and I am worn out".
n.3: Hebrew *ba'ar*, "brutish", as in 12:1.
n.4: Hebrew *binah*, as in 1:2.
n.5: Literally "and the knowledge of the Holy One I know"; the "not" of the first line probably carries over. Or "yet I know the knowledge of the Holy One". *The Holy One* is Hebrew *qedoshim*, as in 9:10.
n.6: Or "if you know!"
n.7: Hebrew *Eloah*, a poetic form of *Elohim*, "God". The line is nearly the same as Psalm 18:31 (18:30 in most English Bibles) and 2 Samuel 22:31.
n.8: Compare Deuteronomy 4:2; 13:1 (12:32 in most English Bibles).
n.9: Literally "the bread of my portion".
n.10: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.11: Literally "A generation", that is, a kind of people. Also in verses 12–14.
n.12: Hebrew *aluqah*, a word found only here, probably "leech".
n.13: The pattern "three … four" builds up to the last item in the list (compare 6:16). Also in verses 18, 21 and 29.
n.14: Hebrew *Sheol*, the realm of the dead.
n.15: Hebrew *yiqqahat*, a rare word, perhaps "obedience" (Genesis 49:10).
n.17: Hebrew *almah*, a young woman old enough to marry (Genesis 24:43; Isaiah 7:14).
n.18: Hebrew *nabal*: a senseless, godless person (see 17:7).
n.19: Hebrew *shefannim*, the rock hyrax, a small animal that lives among rocks (Psalm 104:18).
n.20: Hebrew *semamit*, probably a lizard or gecko; traditionally "spider".
n.22: Hebrew *zarzir motnayim*, literally "girded at the waist", an animal that cannot be identified with certainty: perhaps a rooster, a greyhound or a war horse.
n.23: Hebrew *alqum*, a word of uncertain meaning: perhaps "his army", or "against whom no one rises up".
n.24: In Hebrew *af*, "nose", and *appayim*, "anger" (literally "nostrils"), are the same word.

v: The words of King Lemuel, an oracle[^1] that his mother taught him.
דִּ֭בְרֵי לְמוּאֵ֣ל מֶ֑לֶךְ מַ֝שָּׂ֗א אֲ‍ֽשֶׁר־יִסְּרַ֥תּוּ אִמּֽוֹ׃
What, my son? What, son of my womb? What, son of my vows?[^2]
מַה־בְּ֭רִי וּמַֽה־בַּר־בִּטְנִ֑י וּ֝מֶה בַּר־נְדָרָֽי׃
Do not give your strength to women, your ways to those who destroy kings.
אַל־תִּתֵּ֣ן לַנָּשִׁ֣ים חֵילֶ֑ךָ וּ֝דְרָכֶ֗יךָ לַֽמְח֥וֹת מְלָכִֽין׃
It is not for kings, Lemuel, not for kings to drink wine, nor for rulers to ask, "Where is beer?"[^3]
אַ֤ל לַֽמְלָכִ֨ים ׀ לְֽמוֹאֵ֗ל אַ֣ל לַֽמְלָכִ֣ים שְׁתוֹ־יָ֑יִן וּ֝לְרוֹזְנִ֗ים *או **אֵ֣י שֵׁכָֽר׃
or they will drink and forget what has been decreed and pervert the rights of all the afflicted.
פֶּן־יִ֭שְׁתֶּה וְיִשְׁכַּ֣ח מְחֻקָּ֑ק וִֽ֝ישַׁנֶּה דִּ֣ין כָּל־בְּנֵי־עֹֽנִי׃
Give beer to one who is perishing, and wine to those who are bitter in soul.
תְּנוּ־שֵׁכָֽר לְאוֹבֵ֑ד וְ֝יַיִן לְמָ֣רֵי נָֽפֶשׁ׃
Let them drink and forget their poverty and remember their trouble no more.
יִ֭שְׁתֶּה וְיִשְׁכַּ֣ח רִישׁ֑וֹ וַ֝עֲמָל֗וֹ לֹ֣א יִזְכָּר־עֽוֹד׃
Open your mouth for those who cannot speak, for the rights of all who are destitute.[^4]
פְּתַח־פִּ֥יךָ לְאִלֵּ֑ם אֶל־דִּ֝֗ין כָּל־בְּנֵ֥י חֲלֽוֹף׃
Open your mouth, judge rightly, and defend the rights of the poor and needy.
פְּתַח־פִּ֥יךָ שְׁפָט־צֶ֑דֶק וְ֝דִ֗ין עָנִ֥י וְאֶבְיֽוֹן׃ פ
A capable wife,[^5] who can find? She is worth far more than coral.[^6]
אֵֽשֶׁת־חַ֭יִל מִ֣י יִמְצָ֑א וְרָחֹ֖ק מִפְּנִינִ֣ים מִכְרָֽהּ׃
Her husband's heart trusts in her, and he will not lack gain.[^7]
בָּ֣טַח בָּ֭הּ לֵ֣ב בַּעְלָ֑הּ וְ֝שָׁלָ֗ל לֹ֣א יֶחְסָֽר׃
She does him good and not harm all the days of her life.
גְּמָלַ֣תְהוּ ט֣וֹב וְלֹא־רָ֑ע כֹּ֝֗ל יְמֵ֣י חַיֶּֽיה׃
She seeks out wool and flax and works with willing hands.
דָּ֭רְשָׁה צֶ֣מֶר וּפִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַ֝תַּ֗עַשׂ בְּחֵ֣פֶץ כַּפֶּֽיהָ׃
She is like the merchant ships; she brings her food from far away.
הָ֭יְתָה כָּאֳנִיּ֣וֹת סוֹחֵ֑ר מִ֝מֶּרְחָ֗ק תָּבִ֥יא לַחְמָֽהּ׃
She gets up while it is still night and provides food for her household and portions[^8] for her servant girls.
וַתָּ֤קָם ׀ בְּע֬וֹד לַ֗יְלָה וַתִּתֵּ֣ן טֶ֣רֶף לְבֵיתָ֑הּ וְ֝חֹ֗ק לְנַעֲרֹתֶֽיהָ׃
She considers a field and buys it; from her earnings she plants a vineyard.
זָמְמָ֣ה שָׂ֭דֶה וַתִּקָּחֵ֑הוּ מִפְּרִ֥י כַ֝פֶּ֗יהָ *נטע **נָ֣טְעָה כָּֽרֶם׃
She wraps herself in strength and makes her arms strong.[^9]
חָֽגְרָ֣ה בְע֣וֹז מָתְנֶ֑יהָ וַ֝תְּאַמֵּ֗ץ זְרֹעוֹתֶֽיהָ׃
She sees that her trading is profitable; her lamp does not go out at night.
טָ֭עֲמָה כִּי־ט֣וֹב סַחְרָ֑הּ לֹֽא־יִכְבֶּ֖ה *בליל **בַלַּ֣יְלָה נֵרָֽהּ׃
She puts her hands to the distaff, and her palms grasp the spindle.
יָ֭דֶיהָ שִׁלְּחָ֣ה בַכִּישׁ֑וֹר וְ֝כַפֶּ֗יהָ תָּ֣מְכוּ פָֽלֶךְ׃
She opens her hand to the poor and reaches out her hands to the needy.
כַּ֭פָּהּ פָּרְשָׂ֣ה לֶעָנִ֑י וְ֝יָדֶ֗יהָ שִׁלְּחָ֥ה לָֽאֶבְיֽוֹן׃
She is not afraid of the snow for her household, for all her household are clothed in scarlet.[^10]
לֹא־תִירָ֣א לְבֵיתָ֣הּ מִשָּׁ֑לֶג כִּ֥י כָל־בֵּ֝יתָ֗הּ לָבֻ֥שׁ שָׁנִֽים׃
She makes coverings for herself; her clothing is fine linen and purple.
מַרְבַדִּ֥ים עָֽשְׂתָה־לָּ֑הּ שֵׁ֖שׁ וְאַרְגָּמָ֣ן לְבוּשָֽׁהּ׃
Her husband is known at the city gates, when he sits among the elders of the land.
נוֹדָ֣ע בַּשְּׁעָרִ֣ים בַּעְלָ֑הּ בְּ֝שִׁבְתּ֗וֹ עִם־זִקְנֵי־אָֽרֶץ׃
She makes linen garments and sells them, and supplies sashes to the merchants.[^11]
סָדִ֣ין עָ֭שְׂתָה וַתִּמְכֹּ֑ר וַ֝חֲג֗וֹר נָתְנָ֥ה לַֽכְּנַעֲנִֽי׃
Strength and dignity are her clothing, and she laughs at the time to come.
עֹז־וְהָדָ֥ר לְבוּשָׁ֑הּ וַ֝תִּשְׂחַ֗ק לְי֣וֹם אַחֲרֽוֹן׃
She opens her mouth with wisdom, and loving instruction[^12] is on her tongue.
פִּ֭יהָ פָּתְחָ֣ה בְחָכְמָ֑ה וְתֽ[m]וֹרַת חֶ֝֗סֶד עַל־לְשׁוֹנָֽהּ׃
She watches over the ways of her household and does not eat the bread of idleness.
צ֭וֹפִיָּה הֲלִיכ֣וֹת בֵּיתָ֑הּ וְלֶ֥חֶם עַ֝צְל֗וּת לֹ֣א תֹאכֵֽל׃
Her children rise up and call her happy;[^13] her husband too, and he praises her:
קָ֣מוּ בָ֭נֶיהָ וַֽיְאַשְּׁר֑וּהָ בַּ֝עְלָ֗הּ וַֽיְהַֽלְלָהּ׃
"Many women have done capably,[^14] but you surpass them all."
רַבּ֣וֹת בָּ֭נוֹת עָ֣שׂוּ חָ֑יִל וְ֝אַ֗תְּ עָלִ֥ית עַל־כֻּלָּֽנָה׃
Charm is deceptive and beauty is fleeting,[^15] but a woman who fears the LORD[^16] is to be praised.
שֶׁ֣קֶר הַ֭חֵן וְהֶ֣בֶל הַיֹּ֑פִי אִשָּׁ֥ה יִרְאַת־יְ֝הוָ֗ה הִ֣יא תִתְהַלָּֽל׃
Give her the fruit of her hands, and let her works praise her in the gates.
תְּנוּ־לָ֭הּ מִפְּרִ֣י יָדֶ֑יהָ וִֽיהַלְל֖וּהָ בַשְּׁעָרִ֣ים מַעֲשֶֽׂיהָ׃

n.1: Or "The words of Lemuel king of Massa" (see 30:1). Verses 2–9 are the words of his mother.
n.2: The Hebrew word for "son" here is *bar*, the Aramaic word, used three times in this verse.
n.3: The Hebrew text is written "or beer" but read "Where is beer?"
n.4: Literally "all the sons of passing away", perhaps those who are perishing or have no one to stand up for them.
n.5: Hebrew *eshet chayil*, "a woman of strength, of worth", as in 12:4 and Ruth 3:11. Verses 10–31 form an acrostic poem: each verse begins with the next letter of the Hebrew alphabet, from *aleph* to *tav*.
n.6: Hebrew *peninim*, as in 3:15.
n.7: Literally "plunder".
n.8: Or "tasks".
n.9: Literally "She girds her waist with strength".
n.10: With different vowels, "clothed in double garments", as the Vulgate reads.
n.11: Literally "to the Canaanite", a word that came to mean "trader".
n.12: Literally "the instruction (*torah*) of faithful love (*chesed*)". Or "kind teaching".
n.13: The verb is from the same root as *ashrei*, "happy" (see 3:13).
n.14: Hebrew *chayil*, the word translated "capable" in verse 10. Literally "Many daughters have done capably".
n.15: Hebrew *hevel*, "breath, vapor", the word used throughout Ecclesiastes.
n.16: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
